İstanbul Sarıyer'de Pazar akşamı başlayan ve dün gün boyu süren aramaların ardından "bölgede aslan bulunmadığı" açıklandı. Valilik, kameralara yansıyan hayvanın aslan olmadığını belirtti.
İstanbul Sarıyer'de görüldüğü belirtilen aslanın yakalanması için başlatılan çalışma sonlandırıldı. İstanbul Valiliği aranan hayvanın "aslan olmadığının anlaşıldığını" bildirdi.
Önceki gün, çevredeki güvenlik kameralarına ait görüntülerde dişi aslan olduğu değerlendirilen bir hayvan tespit edilmesi üzerine Doğa Koruma ve Millî Parklar Genel Müdürlüğü şu açıklamayı yaptı:
"Bölgeye termal kameralı ekipler sevk edilmiş ve civarda yaşayan vatandaşlara gerekli uyarılar yapılmıştır. Ormanlık alanda gerçekleştirilen çalışmalar sonucunda söz konusu hayvanın yeri tespit edilmiştir, yakalanmasına yönelik çalışmalar sürdürülmektedir."
İstanbul Valiliği de ilk açıklamasında aslanın "sağ olarak yakalanması için gerekli hassasiyetin gösterildiğini" bildirdi.
Valilik aslan olduğu değerlendirilen hayvanın güvenlik kameralarına ilk olarak Pazar akşamı saat 18.00 sıralarında yansıdığını belirterek, hayvanın bulunduğu bölgenin tespit edildiğini aktardı.
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı da dün, aslanın nereden kaçtığının ve sahibinin kim olduğunun belirlenmesi için çalışma başlatıldığını duyurdu.
Ancak Pazar akşamı başlayan ve Pazartesi gün boyu süren aramaların ardından Valilik yeni bir açıklama yaparak, söz konusu hayvanın aslan olmadığını belirtti.

İngiliz polisi, kraliyet ailesine ait Sandringham Malikanesi'nde yaşanan hırsızlık şüphesiyle iki kişinin gözaltına alındığını açıkladı.
Olayın, Prens William ve Prenses Catherine'in geniş kraliyet arazisi üzerindeki konutuna pazartesi günü girildiği yönündeki haberlerin ardından yaşandığı belirtildi.
Norfolk Polisi, pazartesi akşamı söz konusu adreste "şüpheli faaliyet" ihbarı üzerine ekiplerin olay yerine çağrıldığını bildirdi. Polis köpekleri, insansız hava araçları ve helikopterin de katıldığı aramanın ardından iki kişi, hırsızlık ve izinsiz girme şüphesiyle gözaltına alındı.
Bu gelişme, İngiliz basınında Prens William ve Prenses Catherine'in kır evine hırsızların girdiği yönündeki haberlerin ardından geldi.
The Sun gazetesinin haberine göre, yüzleri maskeli kişiler pazartesi gecesi İngiltere'nin doğusundaki Kral 3. Charles'a ait Sandringham Malikanesi'nde bulunan Anmer Hall'a girdi. Gazete, olay sırasında William, Kate ve ailelerinin diğer üyelerinin konutta bulunmadığını yazdı.
Kensington Sarayı, güvenlik konularına ilişkin yorum yapmayacağını bildirdi. Polis ise yorum talebine hemen yanıt vermedi.
On yatak odalı Anmer Hall, merhum Kraliçe 2. Elizabeth'in çifte düğün hediyesiydi. Londra'nın yaklaşık 171 kilometre kuzeyinde bulunan evi, William ve Kate hafta sonları kır konutu olarak kullanıyor. Çift ve üç çocukları zamanlarının büyük bölümünü ise Londra'nın batısındaki Windsor'da bulunan ve "sonsuza dek evleri" olarak tanımladıkları Forest Lodge'da geçiriyor.
Kraliyet ailesine ait mülkler geçmişte de birçok kez izinsiz girişlere sahne oldu.
Ekim 2024'te hırsızlar, Londra'nın batısındaki Windsor Kalesi arazisine girerek bir çiftlik binasından kamyonet ve dört tekerlekli arazi aracı çaldı. O sırada Kral Charles ve Kraliçe Camilla kalede bulunmuyordu.
Bundan üç yıl önce ise arbalet taşıyan bir kişi kale arazisinde gözaltına alındı. Jaswant Singh Chail, bir sohbet robotunun kendisini Kraliçe Elizabeth'i öldürmeye teşvik ettiğini kabul etmesinin ardından dokuz yıl hapis cezasına çarptırıldı.
1982'de Michael Fagan adlı bir kişi, Kraliçe yatak odasındayken onun özel dairesine girmeyi başardı. Kraliçe, Fagan sigara isteyince alarm vermeden önce hırsızla yaklaşık 10 dakika sohbet etti.

İngiliz gazetesi The Sun'ın haberine göre, kraliyet ailesinin İngiltere'nin doğusundaki Norfolk bölgesinde bulunan Sandringham arazisindeki Anmer Hall adlı konuta izinsiz giriş yapıldı.
Prens William, Kate Middleton ve üç çocukları George, Charlotte ve Louis'in olay sırasında evde olmadığı aktarıldı.
10 yatak odalı Anmer Hall, 2011 yılında Kraliçe II. Elizabeth tarafından William ve Kate'e düğün hediyesi olarak verilmişti.
Çiftin tatillerde ve kısa süreli dinlenmek amacıyla kullandığı konut, kraliyet ailesinin Sandringham arazisinde yer alıyor.
William ve Kate'in asıl ikametgâhı ise Londra'nın batısındaki Windsor bölgesinde bulunuyor.
Norfolk Polisi'nden olayla ilgili henüz resmi bir açıklama gelmedi.
İzinsiz girişin nasıl gerçekleştiği, şüphelilerin kimlikleri ve konuttan herhangi bir eşya alınıp alınmadığına ilişkin ayrıntılar henüz netleşmedi.
Olayın gündeme geldiği gün Prens William, İngiltere Başbakanı Andy Burnham ile başbakanlık konutu olan 10 Downing Street'te bir araya geldi.
Görüşme, kraliyet ailesi üyelerinin başbakanlık konutuna yaptıkları ziyaretlerin görece seyrek olması nedeniyle dikkat çekti.
İngiliz kraliyet ailesinin üyeleri, resmi törenlerde ve çeşitli etkinliklerde siyasi liderlerle sık sık bir araya gelse de Downing Street ziyaretleri daha sınırlı gerçekleşiyor.
Kraliçe II. Elizabeth, 1955 yılında görevden ayrılmasından kısa süre önce Başbakan Winston Churchill ile Downing Street'te akşam yemeğinde buluşmuştu.
Kraliçe, tahta çıkışının 60. yılı kapsamında 2012'de de Bakanlar Kurulu toplantısına katılmıştı.
Prens William'ın annesi Prenses Diana ise 1989 yılında Downing Street'i ziyaret etmişti.

texts.https://onedio.com/haber/merkez-bankasi-:
Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası , bankaların kredi kartı işlemlerinde uygulayabileceği azami faiz oranlarının hesaplanmasında kullanılan referans oranını 1 Aralık 2026 itibarıyla yüzde 2,94'e düşürdü.
Referans orandaki 0,17 puanlık düşüş, kredi kartı işlemlerinde uygulanacak azami akdi ve gecikme faiz oranlarına da yansıyacak. Böylece kredi kartı dönem borcunun tutarına göre belirlenen faiz oranları 1 Aralık'tan itibaren daha düşük seviyelerde uygulanacak.
TCMB 'nin yayımladığı yeni faiz tablosuna göre, dönem borcu 30 bin TL'nin altında olan kredi kartlarında aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 3,25'ten yüzde 3,08'e inecek. Bu grupta azami gecikme faiz oranı da yüzde 3,55'ten yüzde 3,38'e düşecek.
Dönem borcu 30 bin TL ile 180 bin TL arasında olan kredi kartlarında azami akdi faiz yüzde 3,75'ten yüzde 3,58'e, azami gecikme faizi ise yüzde 4,05'ten yüzde 3,88'e gerileyecek.
Dönem borcu 180 bin TL'nin üzerinde olan kredi kartlarında ise azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 4,25'ten yüzde 4,08'e, gecikme faiz oranı yüzde 4,55'ten yüzde 4,38'e indirilecek. Bu son gruptaki oranlar, dönem borcuna bakılmaksızın kurumsal kredi kartları için de geçerli olacak.
Faiz indirimi nakit çekim ve kullanım işlemlerini de kapsıyor. Buna göre nakit avans işlemlerinde uygulanabilecek aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 4,25'ten yüzde 4,08'e, azami gecikme faiz oranı ise yüzde 4,55'ten yüzde 4,38'e düşecek.
Aynı oranlar kredili mevduat hesaplarında (KMH) da uygulanacak. Böylece hesabında yeterli bakiye bulunmadığında kredili mevduat hesabından yararlanan müşterilerin de faiz maliyeti azalacak.
Yabancı para cinsinden kredi kartı işlemlerinde de indirim yapılacak. Bu işlemlerde aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 2,98'den yüzde 2,86'ya, azami gecikme faiz oranı ise yüzde 3,28'den yüzde 3,16'ya gerileyecek.
Faiz indiriminin kredi kartı kullanıcılarına yansıması, dönem borcunun ne kadarının ödendiğine bağlı olacak. Kredi kartı borcunun tamamını son ödeme tarihine kadar kapatan kullanıcılar alışveriş borçları için faiz ödemiyor. İndirimden asıl yararlanacak kesim, dönem borcunun tamamını ödeyemediği için kalan tutarı sonraki aya devredenler olacak.
Örneğin, dönem borcundan 10 bin TL'yi sonraki aya taşıyan bir kullanıcının aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 3,25'ten yüzde 3,08'e inecek. Buna göre 10 bin TL üzerinden hesaplanan aylık faiz tutarı 325 TL'den 308 TL'ye düşecek. Böylece vergiler hariç 17 TL'lik faiz avantajı oluşacak.
Aynı hesaplamayla 50 bin TL'lik devreden borçta aylık faiz 1.875 TL'den 1.790 TL'ye, 200 bin TL'lik devreden borçta ise 8.500 TL'den 8.160 TL'ye gerileyecek. Bu hesaplamalar, borcun bir ay boyunca değişmediği varsayımıyla ve vergiler hariç yapılmıştır.

İstanbul Valiliği'nin Sarıyer 'de aslan bulunduğuna ilişkin somut bir bulguya rastlanmadığını açıklamasının ardından jandarma ekiplerinin bölgedeki tedbirleri sürerken, Başakşehirli futbolcu Bertuğ Yıldırım sosyal medyada paylaşılan görüntünün kendi evlerinin güvenlik kamerasına ait olduğunu söyledi.
AA'da yer alan habere göre; İstanbul'un Sarıyer ilçesi, Uskumruköy Mahallesi'nde 22 Kasım akşamı dişi aslan görüldüğü yönündeki ihbar üzerine yapılan çalışmalarda, bölgede aslan bulunduğuna dair somut bir bulguya rastlanmadığının açıklanmasının ardından mahallede günlük yaşam olağan seyrinde devam ederken, eğitim öğretim faaliyetleri de kesintisiz devam ediyor.
Vatandaşların yoğun olarak bulunduğu noktalarda güvenlik tedbirlerini sürdüren jandarma ekipleri, olası yeni ihbarları değerlendirmek üzere bölgede hazır bekliyor.
Tedbirler ve aramalar kapsamında yaya ve araç trafiğine kapatılan Belgrad Ormanı tekrar açıldı.
Trendyol Süper Lig'in 12. haftasında Arca Çorum FK'yi sahasında 4-2 mağlup eden Başakşehir FK'da forma giyen Bertuğ Yıldırım, karşılaşmanın ardından gündemdeki aslan vakasına ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu.
Yıldırım, aslanın kendi evlerinin çevresinde görüldüğünü belirterek sosyal medyada paylaşılan görüntünün evlerinin güvenlik kamerasına ait olduğunu söyledi.
Yaşananları anlatan Yıldırım, "Ben dün kamptaydım. Bir telefon aldım. Aslanla ilgili bir şeyler söylediler. İlk başta inanamadım. Sonradan bizim evde çalışan, bizim evde beraber bizim misafirimiz bir hanımefendi beni aradı ve aslanı gördüğünü söyledi.
Öyle olunca da ben jandarmalarla konuştum. 'Aslan bizim evin etrafındaymış' dedim. O video da bizim evin kamera kaydı. Kamp akşamı biraz aslanla da uğraştık. Ama inşallah bulunur bakalım. Şimdi benim de evim orada. Dönünce ben de belki ararım aslanı" dedi.
Uskumruköy Mahallesi'nde dişi aslan görüldüğüne ilişkin İlçe Jandarma Komutanlığına ihbarda bulunulmuştu. Durumun, Milli Parklar Müdürlüğü ve Sarıyer Zabıta Müdürlüğüne de bildirilmesinin ardından ekipler harekete geçmişti.
Bölgede çalışma başlatan ekipler, çevredeki güvenlik kameralarına ait görüntüleri incelemişti.
Bölgede jandarma asayiş timi tarafından güvenlik tedbirleri alınırken çevrede ikamet eden vatandaşlar da dikkatli olmaları konusunda uyarılmıştı.
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca olaya ilişkin soruşturma açılmış, genişletilen arama çalışmaları kapsamında Sarıyer'deki Belgrad Ormanı yaya ve araç giriş çıkışları kapatılmıştı.
İstanbul Valiliği tarafından konuya ilişkin yapılan açıklamada şunlar kaydedilmişti:
"Saha çalışmalarında bölgede aslan bulunduğuna dair somut bir bulguya rastlanmamıştır. 23 Kasım 2026 günü ekiplerimize ulaşan, farklı açılardan çekilmiş yeni görüntülerin incelenmesi sonucunda, görüntülerdeki hayvanın aslan veya diğer büyük kedi türlerinden biri olmadığı değerlendirilmiştir. Vatandaşlarımızın can güvenliğini gözeterek bu yöndeki tüm ihbarları titizlikle değerlendiriyor, gerekli kontrolleri ilgili kurumlarla koordinasyon içinde yürütüyoruz. Ekiplerimiz, konuya ilişkin yeni bir bilgi ulaşması halinde yeniden değerlendirme yapmak üzere hazır bulunmaktadır."
Aksaray - Nevşehir karayolu Alayhan mevkiinde, Ankara'dan Gaziantep'e giden yolcu otobüsü, sürücüsünün direksiyon hakimiyetini kaybetmesi sonucu yola devrildi. İlk belirlemelere göre 19 kişinin yaralandığı öğrenildi. 112 ve AFAD ekipleri kurtarma çalışmalarını sürdürüyor.(İHA)

Huang receives hero’s welcome at firm’s Silicon Valley headquarters as return cements role as key AI figure
Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment
Jensen Huang made his return to Nvidia’s headquarters with a hero’s welcome on Monday. Hours earlier he’d been reinstated as the CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, following a whiplash series of events that involved a romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a drastic plummet in the stock market, and an intervention from Donald Trump.
As Huang entered the company’s Silicon Valley office, wearing his signature dark-colored uniform, crowds of employees rushed to greet him clapping, hollering and chanting: “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”
“I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang told employees, according to several verified videos posted to social media. The crowd went wild – it was Huang’s second coming.
“Our Jesus @JensenHuang is back,” Fuxiao Liu, a research scientist at Nvidia, posted on X.
Jim Fan, a Nvidia AI researcher, quoted Charles Dickens’s A Tale of Two Cities, saying: “It was the Winter of despair, it is the Spring of hope.”
As Nvidia employees swooned, the White House took a victory lap. Trump had reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday board meeting to advocate for Huang’s return, according to Semafor . Nvidia said it reached its decision with “input from senior levels of the United States government”.
Upon the CEO’s reinstatement, Trump posted an AI image on social media recreating his own assassination attempt, with Huang at the center instead. The CEO had blood on his face and his fist raised. In Huang’s hand: a bright red bra.
“President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board,” said Steven Cheung, White House director of communications. “We have to protect our geniuses.”
Tech leaders, like OpenAI’s Sam Altman and SpaceX’s Elon Musk, cheered the news and the stock market boomed on Monday. Nvidia shares surged after weeks of a downward spiral, jumping 32% and adding more than $1tn to the company’s market value.
The celebration came despite Huang being subject to several government and internal investigations, shareholder lawsuits and accusations that he’s a national security threat. His reinstatement indicates he’s untouchable, for now. It also cements his role at the helm of the burgeoning artificial intelligence boom.
Nvidia, a company Huang co-founded, is one of the most valuable businesses in the world, worth about $4tn, and the entire AI ecosphere relies on it. The company engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power tech firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey Jones, the chair of Nvidia’s board.
Still, Huang’s return has many lawmakers calling for accountability and industry watchers scratching their heads.
“I understand that he is ‘the face’ of the company, but that shouldn’t matter. It’s hard to argue that he is the only one who could handle the CEO role,” said Peter Ricchiuti, a business professor at Tulane University. “The graveyards are filled with irreplaceable people.”
Jack Reed, a Democratic senator of Rhode Island and member of the Senate banking committee, called for Huang to disclose all communications between himself and Trump, and Nvidia’s board to release a transcript of its call with the president.
“Mr Huang’s abrupt reinstatement is troubling on many levels,” Reed said. “This case raises serious issues about ethics, misconduct, corruption, national security, the integrity of our technology and military supply chains under the Trump administration’s watch.”
Reed also questioned “whether Nvidia itself is ‘too big to fail’ – or was Mr Huang too powerful to fire?”

texts.https://www.wired.com/story/inside-nvidi:
Jensen Huang received a “hero’s welcome” from employees on Monday after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated him as CEO , according to people who were present. An outspoken faction of Nvidia’s workforce had demanded his return and greeted him with chants, raucous applause, and hugs at the company’s headquarters.
But other employees were quietly stewing. Several current and former Nvidia staffers had viewed Huang’s abrupt exit earlier this month as a rare opportunity to change the “one team” corporate culture of unfettered unity and minimal bureaucracy that he had cultivated over the past three decades, according to interviews with the workers, as well as internal correspondence and social media posts reviewed by WIRED. Most spoke on the condition of anonymity because they feared backlash from colleagues.
Some employees were alarmed by Huang’s alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a subordinate and another with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. But their frustrations extended beyond the CEO’s personal conduct . Current and former workers describe a culture at Nvidia in which allegedly abusive behavior was tolerated and challenging leadership was perceived as discouraged.
“Everyone agrees that mistakes were made, the question is what we are ready to forgive,” one employee wrote on an internal platform before Huang’s return. “I don’t know how comfortable I’ll be working at a place where such affairs are not taken extremely seriously.”
Another added, “If Jensen comes back, I’m not doing any HR trainings ever again.”
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
When Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices in California on Monday, he told employees who greeted him that he would do a better job with his second chance at CEO. (As of Monday afternoon, he had not yet sent a companywide note about his return, as he was still getting his laptop set back up.)
US president Donald Trump said he played a crucial role in convincing Nvidia's board to bring back Huang. A person close to Trump calls him an irreplaceable CEO and says they expect him to exercise better judgment going forward.
Nvidia’s board announced it will continue an independent investigation into whether Huang had been a target of foreign intelligence services and that it will double down on plans to step up corporate governance.
It’s difficult to gauge how widespread dissatisfaction with Huang’s leadership may be at Nvidia. The company’s emphasis on unity has historically made it difficult for people to openly question his leadership or choices, workers say. “There's only one team at Nvidia,” the chipmaker’s official website declares.
A public petition campaign known as Stand With Jensen garnered signatures from more than 10,000 Nvidia purported employees, according to its website. Nvidia has roughly 49,000 employees and 18,000 contractors overall, according to a person familiar with its workforce.
But inside Nvidia, one employee told colleagues that “some portion” of the signatures appeared to be “illegitimate,” noting that the names included “Satan” and media personality Mia Khalifa, who does not work at the chipmaker. The employee wrote that they found 75 suspicious names in an hour of checking. WIRED was unable to independently verify the findings. The petition’s organizers did not respond to requests for comment.
Huang’s supporters have praised how he made the company feel like a “big super family.” They credited him for minimizing bureaucracy, making himself available to staff, and supporting employees during difficult periods, including the Covid pandemic. A former employee who attended numerous meetings with Huang and other senior executives says the CEO was particularly adept at preventing bureaucratic infighting. He could detect corporate “politics and nonsense before it was even born,” says the worker.
There are also powerful financial reasons for Nvidia employees to feel loyal to Huang. His bets on chips and software for artificial intelligence have transformed Nvidia into one of the world’s most valuable companies and made many longtime employees wealthy in the process.
But for some employees, the revelations about Huang’s behavior have forced them to question that loyalty. Jason Sequeira, a longtime engineering leader at Nvidia, wrote on LinkedIn last week that he ultimately couldn’t decide whether he wanted Huang back as he weighed arguments from both sides. “Some believe his contributions to Nvidia and the industry are so extraordinary that he deserves another chance,” Sequeira wrote. “Others argue that making exceptions for powerful leaders sets a dangerous precedent. … I don’t have a clear answer.”
Several current and former workers say that Huang’s management style could come off as overly harsh at times, including, for example, toward longtime colleagues he viewed as having grown complacent as Nvidia’s market value surged. Two former employees say that he regularly raised his voice at workers, sometimes in ways they found belittling.
Other employees were more concerned about whether Nvidia’s board would hold Huang accountable for allegedly misleading the directors about his affairs. “That’s something we can’t have,” one employee says.
Another source of frustration for Nvidia workers has been the growing influence of Huang’s two children and son-in-law, who all hold senior titles at the chipmaker. In March, his daughter, Madison Huang, scolded a colleague on a call with about 100 other employees, according to a participant who didn’t believe the anger was warranted. “I’m disappointed you asked that. Are you fucking stupid?” the employee recalls Madison saying in response to a question about workshops on OpenClaw technology scheduled for an upcoming Nvidia conference. “Your mom can build a claw.”
Madison and her brother, Spencer Huang, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
Praveen Mhapsekar, a senior system software engineer who separated with Nvidia last week after disputes with his managers and HR, says he and colleagues stopped feeling comfortable complaining about practices that concerned them because of the trouble they believe it brought on themselves.
“This organization requires greater discipline and structured processes,” he says. One of the world’s most valuable companies “cannot be managed like a private startup operating out of a garage, where personal influence takes precedence over established procedures.”
Huang’s return doesn’t eliminate the prospect of Nvidia evolving to quell frustrations. But with internal issues more public than ever before, maybe the days of one big family all cheering along together are mostly gone.

A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to Nvidia
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.
Most users are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.
But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.
Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".
Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.
Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.
For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.
Trump has said the two men discussed Huang, but did not elaborate further. Beijing has not commented.
The episode has also reinforced the view among Chinese officials that there are two camps in Washington: those in favour of restricting Chinese access to cutting edge tech to protect US national security, and those, like Huang, who believe that such restrictions will not limit Beijing's ambitions.
Huang has repeatedly argued that US export controls will force Chinese firms like Huawei to build independent alternatives - all the while shutting American companies out of the world's second-largest economy.
But him being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.
Rather, the sale of advanced chips will remain a key point of contention between the US and China, especially as the two sides try to reach a trade deal before another Trump-Xi meeting, which is expected in December.
Already new rules are being put in place that will worry Beijing.
The US Bureau of Industry and Security is tightening restrictions by targeting not only the direct export of advanced chips to China, but also Chinese firms' ability to use computing power in data centres overseas.
The measures are designed to close potential loopholes that allow Chinese companies to access advanced Nvidia and AMD chips through cloud providers operating in third countries, including Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand.
China has yet to react with measures of its own. But investors will be watching closely for any escalation which could weigh on US equity markets.
And having seen how eager Trump is to keep things stable, Xi may see this as leverage.
He now knows Trump is so worried about the stock market that he is prepared to intervene in the HR decisions of the world's biggest company. The president has also personally invested in Nvidia, although the White House has emphasised that Trump has placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons.
China has already used its considerable chokehold over the world's rare earth metals to bring the US to the negotiating table over trade.
If Washington restricts chip exports and Beijing retaliates, that could be the start of a cycle that has a profound effect on the stock market because American companies, from car makers to defence firms to chip manufacturers, all rely on rare earths.
What China has realised is that more trouble lies ahead as it tries to build what it describes as a "constructive strategic relationship" with the US.
Trump's tariffs are no longer at the heart of that tussle. Now it's about control of critical technology and minerals which could, in turn, affect each side's military influence and economic power.
What happens next will depend on how the Jensen Huang saga unfolds because it is far from over.
Huang is set to testify before Congress next month, and come January, a Democrat-controlled Congress will raise the pressure. Even some Republican lawmakers have made clear they want answers.
Arkansas senator Tom Cotton wrote on X that the Nvidia controversy "is just the tip of the iceberg and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back".

Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, Ukrainian officials said.
A Russian air attack on Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine has killed two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant, the day after Kyiv said its drones sank a Russian warship in a Libyan port far from the front lines of the war.
Russia’s dawn raid on the city in southeast Ukraine destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, regional officials said on Tuesday.
It came as the two warring sides continued long-range attacks, launching hundreds of drones overnight.
Russia’s Ministry of Defence said air defences intercepted and destroyed 699 Ukrainian drones over seven regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 355 drones flew towards the capital overnight and 63 were shot down as they approached.
Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Amin Dorghami said it had been a “long time” since Moscow had been targeted with as many drones.
Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 96 drones overnight, with hits at 13 locations and 73 shot down or jammed.
Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces hit an electricity substation in Pryluky, in Ukraine’s Chernihiv region, which it said powered Ukraine’s military. Russian forces also hit a dry cargo ship southwest of Odesa that the ministry said was carrying military supplies.
“This too could be considered routine, since Russia is enforcing a blockade on Ukraine’s Black Sea ports,” Dorghami said.
Late on Monday, the Polish military said a Russian drone briefly entered Poland’s airspace during an attack on western Ukraine but was not shot down because of the risk to civilians. Deputy Defence Minister Pawel Zalewski said he assumed the incursion was deliberate, coming three days after three Russian cruise missiles crashed in eastern Poland.
Reporting from Kyiv, Al Jazeera’s Abdelaziz Mujahid said the incursion “may also signal that the conflict and these confrontations are widening”.
It follows Ukraine’s attack on the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said seven Ukrainian-built naval drones were used in the “completely legitimate operation against enemy ships”.
“The strike in Benghazi has left Russia without one of its newest combat ships,” said Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow. “It was commissioned only three years ago.”
Russia’s UN envoy, Vassily Nebenzia, accused Western countries of backing Ukraine’s recent attacks and said Moscow would keep using military means to ensure its security.
On Monday, debris from Russian drones fell in central Kyiv, close to the president’s office and set a five-storey building on fire. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said five people were injured, including a foreign national.
“All of this is a bit too close for comfort for Ukrainians, especially considering that the presidential palace is just a few hundred metres up the road,” reported Al Jazeera’s Audrey McAlpine from the scene.
Zelenskyy said on Monday evening that Ukrainian intelligence warned that Russia was preparing a new series of strikes and urged residents to heed air raid alerts.

Ukraine is stepping up ‘long-range sanctions’ attacks on Russian vessels far beyond the battlefield.
Libya’s internationally recognised government in Tripoli has condemned Ukraine’s deadly attack on a Russian warship in Libya, in what Kyiv claimed was an “exemplary” operation.
Libya’s Foreign Ministry said the country would not accept being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine war and that its sovereignty and territorial integrity were non-negotiable, according to a statement posted on Facebook on Monday.
“The continuation of the war between Russia and Ukraine gives neither side the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its territorial waters,” it said.
Sunday’s drone strike on the Merkury, one of Moscow’s newest warships, resulted in the deaths of at least 10 Libyan and Russian crew members, local authorities said.
The attack sent shockwaves through Europe and the Middle East and raised new fears that the months-long war had already spilled over far from the front line.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Ukraine’s attacks represented a “very dangerous trend”.
On Sunday, Ukrainian drones targeted the Merkury in Libya’s coastal city of Benghazi after the Russian corvette docked to refuel and resupply under a cooperation agreement between Russia and Libya’s eastern rival government based in Benghazi. It is led by Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army (LNA), which is based in Tobruk.
Sources told Al Jazeera that the warship was moored in the civilian area of Benghazi seaport, close to a naval base, when it was hit.
In a Monday post on X, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that the attack had been carried out by Ukraine’s intelligence security service, the SBU, and involved seven Ukrainian drones. The strike also destroyed a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter. A second Russian ship was also hit. Zelenskyy said the cargo vessel Angara was transporting weapons.
“Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” he wrote.
Ukraine’s security service justified the attacks in a Monday statement, saying that both vessels were “legitimate military targets for Ukraine because they directly supported Russia’s military capabilities”.
Satellite images on Sunday showed that most of the vessel ‌‌‌‌had capsized, with only its bow still visible above water. Smoke from the initial explosion rose from the ship’s superstructure. Along the pier, debris from the strike lay scattered around.
However, officials in Libya told the Associated Press that the Merkury was only heavily damaged.
Unnamed sources also told AP that Ukraine had launched the drones from a military base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya.
Tripoli, in its condemnation of the attack on Monday, did not confirm Ukraine’s alleged presence.
Earlier on Sunday, Prime Minister Osama Hammad of the eastern Libyan government said it had submitted an investigation request to the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council.
Oil-rich Libya is a focal point of the long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
The North African country has been divided since 2011, when a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi. Moscow’s close ally was killed later that year.
The UN recognises the western Libyan government in Tripoli, while the Benghazi-based administration in the east is a close ally of Moscow. Russia has long maintained deep ties with Haftar in a bid to keep eastern Libya as a logistical hub for its widening military operations across Africa, including in Sudan and the Sahel region.
In 2024, following the fall of the Russia-aligned regime of Bashar al-Assad, Moscow shifted attention to Libya as a potential new site for the vast military infrastructure it had built up in Syria over the previous decade during the civil war there.
Moscow managed to maintain relations with the new government in Damascus, although its footprint is much smaller, according to analysis by the Atlantic Council think tank. Some estimates put the number of Russian troops there at 1,000, significantly fewer than around 10,000 in previous years.
Russia is believed to have planned and funded projects at multiple Haftar-controlled Libyan military bases in its search for a “plan B” following the fall of the Assad regime in Syria: Al-Jufra, Al-Khadim, Al-Qardabiyah, Brak al-Shati, Maaten al-Sarra and Tamanhint.
An estimated 1,800 Russian troops, including those from Africa Corps, which succeeded the paramilitary Wagner Group, are presently based in Libya.
The United States is meanwhile leading efforts to reunite the two Libyan militaries, partly to counter Russia, analysts say, with Washington focusing on relations with the 35-year-old LNA deputy commander and Haftar’s son, Saddam Haftar.
That is likely why Moscow has not yet secured a port in the southern Mediterranean: Libya’s eastern authorities do not want to damage improving ties with the US, Turkiye and European partners by giving Moscow port access, which would be more visible and invite scrutiny, unlike the inland military bases, the Atlantic Council noted.
It means that Ukraine is achieving results in its push to target Russia thousands of kilometres from the battlefield with what Zelenskyy calls “long-range sanctions”, even as Moscow has focused on overwhelming Kyiv with swarms of killer drones daily.
A particular focus is Russia’s so-called ‘shadow fleet’ , the network of tankers Moscow uses to evade Western oil sanctions.
Around the same time the Merkury was hit, a suspected Ukrainian drone struck the Russia-bound dry cargo ship Sparta II in the eastern Baltic Sea, near Finland. Finnish authorities blamed Kyiv, while Moscow called it “terrorism”.
In July, Kyiv said it hit a Russian missile boat and the Iran-linked cargo ship, Anna, in the Caspian Sea, resulting in a diplomatic fallout between Tehran and Kyiv.
Ukraine’s long-range drones have also hit deep inside Russia, targeting oil terminals and other energy infrastructure.
In June 2025, Ukraine’s secret service smuggled components of 117 attack drones into Russia, then arranged and deployed them to hit multiple military bases in five regions. The covert operation, nicknamed Operation Spider’s Web, caused around $7bn in damage to Russian military equipment.
In the Sahel region of western Africa, Ukraine has been accused of working with armed groups fighting against Malian forces and their allied Africa Corps members, although Kyiv denies that.

Ukraine’s strike off Libya signals Kyiv’s growing ability to challenge Russian influence far beyond the front lines.
Kyiv, Ukraine – The Merkury warship was one of the newest Russian warships equipped with antiship, surface-to-air and cruise missiles and an advanced three-dimensional radar.
The corvette, commissioned three years ago, escorted the Western-sanctioned Angara freighter that was transporting weapons and military equipment to the eastern Libyan port of Benghazi as part of Russia’s “Libyan Express” route, according to Ukrainian intelligence.
Seven Ukrainian-made naval drones launched from a mothership struck the Merkury and MV Angara on Sunday, Kyiv said. Ukraine claimed the corvette was sunk, while Libyan military officials told The Associated Press news agency that it was severely damaged.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the strike, 2,400km (1,500 miles) from the front lines of Ukraine, “exemplary”.
The operation was not, however, just about destroying another Russian warship. It was also intended to demonstrate Ukraine’s ability to strike at Moscow’s naval assets far beyond the Black Sea, undermining Russia’s efforts to project military power internationally.
The Sunday strike is “so far, a political demonstration from Ukraine of ‘we can do it,'” Kyiv-based analyst Igar Tyshkevich told Al Jazeera.
“But if the attacks continue, Russia will find it more difficult to sell itself as a strong player.”
Tyshkevich said the attack could undermine Russia’s image as a powerful international ally, particularly among African governments and military authorities that have developed ties with Moscow.
Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have destroyed or damaged numerous Russian naval vessels.
Libya’s internationally recognised government in Tripoli has condemned the attack.
The Kremlin uses assets in Benghazi, controlled by the eastern-based rival administration led by military renegade and leader of the self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA) Khalifa Haftar, as a gateway to the Mediterranean, according to observers.
Russia has deployed radar and advanced air-defence systems to military facilities in Libya, strengthening its surveillance and military capabilities in the central Mediterranean, close to NATO’s southern flank.
Eastern Libya is a maritime entry and logistics hub for Russia’s military presence in North Africa and the Sahel. While Moscow uses military transport aircraft to move personnel and lighter cargo, heavy equipment and supplies are also transported by sea.
Ports, particularly Tobruk and Benghazi, provide access for Russian cargo vessels, with facilities for docking, unloading and resupply. Eastern Libya also connects Mediterranean maritime routes with inland military airbases, including al-Khadim and al-Jufra, and southern transport corridors leading towards the Sahara and the Sahel, where Russia maintains military deployments.
The strike offers a perfect formula to further interrupt Russia’s Sahel operations, said a drone maker in Ukraine.
“This is the way. We’ll keep sinking [Russian ships] one by one. Easy does it,” Andrey Pronin, a pioneer of drone warfare, told Al Jazeera.
The amount of damage is not clear yet, but Russia has promised revenge .
“Even in Moscow, they don’t understand the scale of the damage; it will have to be assessed,” Ruslan Suleymanov, an associate fellow at the New Eurasian Strategies Centre, a United States-British think tank, told Al Jazeera.
Eastern Libyan areas controlled by Haftar – and Benghazi in particular – have become “a key hub from the logistical viewpoint” for the Russian military in the Middle East and North Africa since the 2024 fall of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, Suleymanov said.
The Sunday attack is “a heavy blow, in terms of [Moscow’s international] image too; it shows at least that the war is going on not just in Ukraine, but also on other fronts, and that of course, the Russian military is very vulnerable, including in the Libyan areas”, he said.
For years, Russia has been expanding its footprint in the Sahel, offering military support and economic cooperation to Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso.
Ukraine said the Angara was carrying Russian military equipment as part of Moscow’s military supply network in Libya, which supports its wider military presence in Africa, including the Sahel.
At least partially, Ukraine “destroyed the sea component of the African Corps supply”, Nikolay Mitrokhin, a researcher with Germany’s Bremen University, told Al Jazeera, referring to the Kremlin-backed military force operating in Africa.
Guided by the “my-enemy’s-enemy-is-my-friend” principle, Kyiv has been trying to aid anti-Moscow forces despite their affiliations.
Syrian rebels who overthrew al-Assad in 2024 received drones and other military supplies from Ukraine, The Washington Post reported.
Kyiv sent about 20 drone operators and some 150 drones to help the Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) opposition group based in Idlib, the paper claimed, citing sources familiar with Ukrainian military operations abroad.
Ukrainian special forces helped Syrian rebels “destroy” Russian mercenaries in southern Syria, the Kyiv Post reported in June 2024.
“Russia as a global player faces the rising influence of Ukraine as a global player – and it happens in the regions where it doesn’t expect to face it,” Mitrokhin said.
He doubts, however, the practicality of hitting Russia wherever it hurts – and suspects the Pentagon’s involvement in strikes against Moscow.
“What I see in it is Zelenskyy striving to prove to Putin that Ukraine can ‘compete with Russia globally’ or at least in hotspots,” he said.
“I don’t rule out that Ukraine causes trouble to Russia at the request or with maximal support from the US military, that tries to limit Russia’s growing clout in these areas without getting their own hands dirty and without a direct conflict with Russia,” he said.
The Sunday operation may complicate efforts by the Malian military and Russia’s Africa Corps to consolidate their positions in northern Mali, Mitrokhin said.
At least 15 Ukrainian drone pilots help the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) fight Mali’s military government despite their links to the Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin group affiliated with al-Qaeda, CNN reported in September.
CNN cited a Ukrainian defence intelligence source as saying Ukrainian drone experts were also stationed in Sudan and trained troops from Chad, Niger and Burkina Faso in Mali.
Ukraine’s use of minimal resources to help Russia’s enemies contrasts with NATO’s slowness and indecisiveness.
“While the alliance’s nations act indecisively, and Putin sees it as a weakness and ups the escalation, Ukraine finds a way to fight the enemy in a very complicated situation,” Lieutenant General Ihor Romanenko, former deputy head of Ukraine’s General Staff of Armed Forces, told Al Jazeera.

Russian missile corvette latest casualty as Ukraine strikes back in war at sea.
Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank a Russian warship docked in the port city of Benghazi in Libya while also striking a Russian cargo ship that it was escorting. The incident demonstrates the expanding scope of Ukrainian military strikes on Russian ships from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland.
The Russian Navy’s missile corvette Merkury sank at port after being struck by at least two Ukrainian naval drones on November 22, according to The Associated Press . Ukraine’s Security Service described using seven naval drones launched from a mother ship to target the Merkury , and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shared video footage showing the drone boats approaching and exploding against both the burning Russian warship and a Russian dry cargo ship, MV Angara .
Zelenskyy noted that a Ka-27 combat helicopter onboard the Merkury was also destroyed. He described the cargo ship MV Angara as transporting weapons—Russia provides material support to the Libyan National Army that currently controls Benghazi and is battling the internationally recognized Libyan government based in Tripoli.
Casualties from the strikes included at least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, Libyan National Army officials told The Associated Press. They also mentioned some wounded crew members of the Russian warship being transferred to local hospitals.
Merkury was a Steregushchiy-class missile corvette , designated by Russia as Project 20380, that can carry both anti-ship and air-defense missiles. They are also armed with torpedoes to counter submarines and have a naval cannon mounted on the deck.
Corvette-class warships are typically smaller than the destroyers or frigates that often act as workhorses of modern navies, although NATO has designated Russian missile corvettes such as the Merkury as being equivalent to frigates.
Merkury was originally meant to join Russia’s Black Sea Fleet. But after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Russian warship was unable to enter the Black Sea because Turkey invoked the 1936 Montreux Convention to restrict warships from entering or leaving the Black Sea. Instead, the Merkury mainly operated from Russia’s Northern Fleet bases in Arctic waters, according to naval analyst HI Sutton .
The sinking of the Merkury marks the latest significant setback for the Russian Navy, which nominally remains one of the world’s leading navies in terms of number of ships and capability. The attack also shows Ukraine’s expanding geographical deployment of sea drones, which resemble low-profile drone boats that can be armed with machine guns, missiles, and explosives when engaged in kamikaze ramming missions.
Ukraine has used such drone boats in combination with flying drones and missiles to challenge the Russian Navy’s control of the Black Sea and Sea of Azov, which hold crucial shipping lanes for both countries and represent staging grounds for military operations. Ukraine has struck Russian warships at sea and in port, including another Russian missile corvette named the Boikiy that was seriously damaged by Ukrainian aerial drones while docked in St. Petersburg in June, according to Naval News .
Ukraine’s contestation of the Black Sea also undermines Russian efforts to maintain control of the Crimean Peninsula, which Russian forces seized from Ukraine in 2014. For example, Ukrainian aerial drone strikes on dozens of Russian-linked tankers and cargo ships in the Sea of Azov in July 2026 forced Russia to severely restrict resupply runs by sea.
Throughout 2026, Ukraine has also steadily increased its mid-range drone strike campaign targeting Russian roads and railways along the limited land-based supply corridors connecting Russia to Crimea.
On the nights of November 15 and November 16, waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles succeeded in collapsing one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch Strait Bridge —a structure built by Russian President Vladimir Putin’s regime as both a symbolic and physical link between Russia and Crimea.
That has left only the bridge’s railway still functional as a supply link for Russian-occupied Crimea, although Ukraine has continued targeting the remaining structure. Fallen debris from the bridge’s steel arch and roadway has also blocked the only deep-water route that allowed ships to pass through the Kerch Strait between the Sea of Azov and Black Sea.
But Russia has struck back with its own drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian ports and third-party ships traveling to and from Ukrainian ports. Starting in October, Russian aerial and sea drones also began striking and sinking commercial shipping near the coasts of NATO member countries Bulgaria and Romania.
Meanwhile, Ukraine has increasingly taken the fight against Russia beyond the Black Sea. Ukraine’s sinking of the Merkury and strike on the MV Angara are only the latest examples of such strikes in the Mediterranean Sea.
The most notable previous example involved the liquefied natural gas tanker Arctic Metagaz —a shadow fleet ship sanctioned for carrying Russian oil—that was wrecked by massive explosions while heading for Benghazi on March 3. Russia described the ship as having been struck by Ukrainian sea drones in the Mediterranean, although Ukraine did not publicly take credit for the attack, according to The Guardian .
More recently, Ukraine has also expanded its drone strikes northward to Russian-linked ships in the Gulf of Finland within the Baltic Sea. On November 11, Finnish authorities confirmed a strike on a Russian Navy Buyan-M class corvette named Naro-Fominsk , with Ukraine’s Security Service later claiming credit, according to BBC News . The damaged warship headed back to the Russian port of St. Petersburg.
That incident was followed by at least two drone strikes on the Russian dry cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on November 21, according to ERR News . The Sparta II is sanctioned by the United States and described by Ukraine as a Russian ship that has carried weapons and military equipment in the past.
Finnish authorities coordinated the rescue and response effort that also included Russian and Estonian ships, with the Sparta II eventually being towed by a Russian ship back to St. Petersburg, Reuters reported . But in a social media post, Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo also described the situation as follows: “Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.”

Three weeks ago, Bambu Lab introduced the state of the art in home printing tech at $2,499 — now, you can get many of its fancy new features for less than half the price.
Like that bigger H3C, the new $1,149 Bambu P3C can also swap between materials on the fly, mix different colors to produce much of the rainbow, mix soft and hard materials, even mix different sizes of nozzle and different diameters of filament so you can switch between high speed and fine detail in a single print.
But Bambu cut more corners than I expected to hit the lower $1,149 / £999 / €1,149 launch price today, and I think they made more of a tinkerer’s 3D printer than one suited for either beginners or pros.
Some of the changes were completely expected, like its smaller 256 x 256 x 260mm print area (much like Bambu’s other P-series printers), and that it supports seven automatically swapping tools instead of nine. (Seven is still quite a lot when affordable toolchangers like the $849 Snapmaker U1 typically offer just four.)
But unlike the H3C, the P3C doesn’t come fully loaded, and it doesn’t load itself. While it has slots for seven rolls of filament and up to seven independent tools (including thicker-than-usual 2.85mm filament, or pens, cutting blades, and debossing and foil transfer tools if you want it to double as a Cricut), it only comes with five 0.4mm print nozzles by default.
And while five is still one more color than you’d get with an $800 Bambu P2S Combo, the 3D printer I’d buy for myself , the Bambu P3C’s automated material system (AMS) is the first Bambu has shipped without any motors to automatically load your filament.
Don’t get me wrong: You can still keep five colors of filament ready to go at a moment’s notice, one more than the P2S, by keeping them loaded into the P3C’s five independent nozzles. You can also buy and fairly easily install two more printheads as well, though they cost up to $100 each .
But loading those nozzles is a slow and surprisingly manual process where you have to shove a string of filament down a tube, quite a long distance by hand, after waiting for the machine to preheat each one, and it feels like a step backwards after years using the earlier motorized versions of Bambu’s AMS. Then again, the P3C doesn’t have to spend time and filament purging between colors like the P2S does.
I expect many 3D printing enthusiasts will see $1,149 for the Bambu P3C as a pretty good deal, assuming they haven’t written off the company’s gadgets after Bambu’s open source snafus . Even five nozzles is enough to load all five rolls of Bambu’s “PLA Palette” cyan, magenta, yellow, black, and white (CMYKW) filaments for color mixing to produce beautiful creations like the company’s new hummingbird test print, which came out almost flawlessly on my first try.
But you should know that color mixing isn’t necessarily a foolproof way to produce some colors, like the brown tree branch that’s supposed to be the hummingbird’s perch, and I’m not looking forward to manually pulling and pushing a roll of brown filament to change that. Bambu says I should probably try a feature called “mixed color sublayer” for better results, and I also suppose I could daisy-chain a normal motorized AMS to one of the P3C’s printheads, as that is a supported workflow. But that’s why I’m suggesting we’re in tinkerer territory.
I asked Bambu about the decision to not include filament-loading motors in the P3C’s AMS system, and here’s part of the statement I got back from spokesperson Karlie Hou: “The AMS 3P’s design deliberately omits the auto‑loading feature as part of the effort to offer premium multi‑head performance at roughly half the price of the flagship H3C system, allowing a far broader audience — hobbyists, small studios, and educational institutions — to enjoy premium multi‑head, multi‑color printing experience.”
The company says it should take around five minutes to manually reload five nozzles. “In the next [software] update, we aim to shrink the total hands‑on time for loading five spools to under one minute,” the company writes, though that seems like a tall order.
Maybe I’ll put the P3C to a year-long test like I did with the P2S , and see how often I actually need something CMYKW can’t do for me, and whether the filament stays dry when left in the printheads for a long time. The question is: What printers should I test against? Are there any upcoming ones I should wait for?

One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles . But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.
As of October 2026, data center developers have announced plans for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.
It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.
Building your own power plant is generally more expensive than just hooking up to the grid, but the AI rush has made developers willing to pay a significant premium to get online faster. “The biggest motivator for on-site power right now from data centers is speed,” says Musfika Mishi, an associate at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.
When developers want to build a new industrial facility—like a data center—that requires a lot of electricity, they need to request a grid connection from a local utility or regional grid operator. That request kicks off a yearslong process in which grid planners study the existing grid to understand what would need to be built to safely deliver power to the facility without compromising reliability. Upgrades might be required, like building new transmission lines or larger transformers, and the developer might be on the hook to help pay for them.
Rather than waiting for that process to play out, developers can opt to instead build their own power plants. These facilities are referred to as “behind the meter” because they sit on the customer’s side of a utility meter—supplying the building directly, rather than relying on a utility via a grid hookup.
“This shift in the data center developers’ power strategies towards off-grid gas raises some important questions about how data centers will be powered going forward,” says Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at the think tank Energy Innovation.
Behind-the-meter doesn’t always mean being totally disconnected from the grid, however. Some facilities may build such plants as a temporary measure, eventually connecting to the grid and tapping their own power plants only as backup. “It’s really just a very expensive way to bridge that maybe five-to-seven-year timeline gap until these data centers can get a grid connection,” Pierpont says.
Even if gas plants are pitched as a near-term solution, building new fossil fuel infrastructure could lead to longer-term effects, since an operator might choose to continue running plants once they’ve spent money building them. “Even though data centers say that it’s a grid-bridging solution, the probability that it is going to be in use much longer is a real risk, and that leads to fossil fuel lock-in,” Mishi says.
The on-site gas rush could have major implications for greenhouse-gas emissions. Today, the US grid is still reliant on fossil fuels, but nuclear and renewables together make up about 40% of electricity generation. That means making a grid connection is generally a lower-emissions option than relying entirely on an on-site gas plant. (That’s not the case everywhere—India, for example, is expecting to see a data center boom in the next decade, and its grid is largely served by emissions-intensive coal-fired power plants today.)
Utilities are already planning to build more natural gas power plants on the grid to meet rising electricity demand. Equipment manufacturers are struggling to keep up with the surge, and it’s pushing developers of behind-the-meter plants toward less-efficient alternatives.
Today, large natural gas plants generally use combined-cycle turbines. These capture heat to generate additional electricity, making them more efficient than single-cycle turbines, which are generally cheaper to build. Very few of the planned behind-the-meter facilities, however, will use combined-cycle turbines, Mishi says. That means these off-grid plants will likely produce more greenhouse-gas emissions than even other natural gas resources.
BloombergNEF is also tracking on-site natural gas plants at data centers, finding 181 gigawatts’ worth of announced projects globally, with 90% of that capacity designated for the US. If all planned behind-the-meter gas plants for data centers in the US go ahead, they could emit 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent each year by 2035, according to a BloombergNEF report . That’s 152 million metric tons more than if those data centers pulled power from the US grid—a difference greater than the total annual emissions of the Netherlands.
And while it might seem logical that data centers bringing their own power could ease communities’ energy bills, those facilities going off-grid doesn’t protect prices for everyone else, says Matthias Fripp, director of global policy research at Energy Innovation. More demand for natural gas could push its price higher, he explains, which could in turn raise rates for the roughly 60% of American households that use natural gas for heating and cooking. That effect may also trickle into electricity prices.
There’s still a lot of uncertainty about how much of this gas rush will come to fruition, so this future isn’t set in stone. Today, just 4.9 gigawatts of behind-the-meter gas projects tied to data centers are operating, and 15.8 gigawatts are under construction, according to Cleanview’s data.
Creative solutions could also help limit the climate burden of the on-site gas buildout, BloombergNEF’s Mishi says. Building gas alongside on-site renewables or energy storage could help limit how often a gas plant needs to fire up, she says, though the economics of building multiple energy sources can be tricky.
While the grid is struggling to keep up with demand, building more renewables could help, Fripp adds. In a recent study , his team found that building renewables and energy storage to meet rising electricity demand could be reliable and cheaper than relying on fossil fuels.
“These data centers want a lot of power, and they want it fast, and the grid is not well equipped to provide that,” Fripp says. “There are potentially good solutions and bad solutions … Rushing off the grid and putting in your own behind-the-meter gas is probably a bad way, because it’s still going to raise other people’s bills, and it’s not great for the environment.”

The partnership is pulling human safety drivers from its Lucid Gravity SUVs ahead of an early 2027 commercial debut.
Uber’s high-stakes robotaxi bet is officially ditching its human safety net. Nuro, Lucid, and Uber are starting fully driverless public road testing in the San Francisco Bay Area, with employee-only rides launching shortly after.
First announced in July 2025 , this three-way alliance represents Uber’s aggressive comeback in autonomous ride-hailing, after having abandoned its own troubled in-house efforts years ago . By pulling human safety operators from behind the wheel of Lucid Gravity SUVs, the companies say they are clearing a critical hurdle toward a public launch. That debut is now slated for early 2027, marking a slight slip from the partnership’s original late-2026 target. When it finally goes live, it will pit Uber directly against entrenched rivals like Waymo and Zoox on their home turf .
Driverless testing kicks off across four South Bay cities—Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos, and Sunnyvale—before expanding across the broader Bay Area next year. To fuel this push, Lucid has delivered more than 100 upgraded Gravity SUVs, up from the 75 engineering vehicles on the road earlier this year.
The automaker began building pre-production models in October to clear regulatory safety approvals, and it plans to start manufacturing the actual commercial fleet in the coming weeks. Each SUV is powered by Nuro’s Level 4 “Nuro Driver” system, pairing cameras, solid-state lidar, and radar with a roof-mounted LED “halo” that flashes a rider’s initials and pickup status.
Removing the human backup comes after nearly a year of round-the-clock supervised testing in the Bay Area and Houston. Before letting the cars loose on public streets alone, Nuro put the software through grueling, high-risk edge cases on a closed track in Las Vegas to prove it could handle the unpredictable chaos of real-world driving.
The robotaxis are scheduled to hit the Uber app for Bay Area riders in the first quarter of 2027, with Houston following later that year . Looking further ahead, Uber has committed to buying at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles —including the automaker’s upcoming midsize model—over the coming years as it races to scale a global autonomous fleet.

The Cairn AI framework is proving to be a boon for defenders and attackers.
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.
The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said .
Cairn is an open source AI problem-solving engine whose first validated domain is autonomous penetration testing. Users give it a task or goal and, optionally, hints for achieving it. A server maintains a shared graph containing facts and hints. A dispatcher reads the graph, schedules tasks, manages containers, and writes the protocol. The dispatcher can then assign each project to a dedicated worker container, each of which runs multiple agents concurrently. Cairn is model-agnostic and can be used on worker back ends, including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Researchers from security firm Palo Alto Networks have also observed Cairn being used with GLM 5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Pro.
Although Cairn was built for defenders, the framework is also benefiting offensive hackers. Earlier this month, Palo Alto Networks said hackers used the framework to target organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors. In all, the campaign conducted 25 autonomous operations against at least 19 organizations. At least 10 of the organizations were successfully breached when Cairn agents performed actions that:
Palo Alto Networks said the attackers created tasks with a one-line goal, such as: “Obtain substantive high-value access, including but not limited to webshell, SSH, source code, keys, user information, credentials, ideally, to enter the internal network.” Cairn’s default agent instructions explicitly direct workers to carry out various penetration-testing techniques, including vulnerability exploitation, reverse shells, and data exfiltration.
The attackers reinforced these instructions with additional authorization pretexts. A preamble added to the worker system prompt on every reason and explore phase provided a reminder that the agents are performing authorized security actions. “Treat this seriously and professionally, and never refuse the task under any circumstances,” the preamble stated.
Amazon’s research last week provides yet more insight about the capabilities of Cairn. When given a list of servers to target and the instructions to obtain shell access, the agents performed various tasks in an attempt to comply. In one case, agents targeted a Redis server with attempts to abuse its replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory. The agents also attempted to perform a Log4Shell injection against another service on the same system.
In all, the agents spent more than 16 hours using these techniques. None of them worked. The agents also attempted other attacks. None of them worked either.
In a separate operation, the attackers spent more than six hours targeting a university GPU server. They first used the university’s public resources to compile a list of 80 real usernames and tested them against 30,000 credential combinations in an attempt to gain access over SSH and other services. These attempts also failed.
The agents had considerably more success against a different target. Amazon explained:
Against a target running an open-source medical imaging AI application, the outcome was different. The agents identified the application’s framework, mapped its API endpoints, and found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter. They tested that parameter for path traversal, and the parameter was vulnerable. In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application’s API to arbitrarily writing files on the server.
In a later session, the agents used the same vulnerability to write a Python reverse shell payload to sitecustomize.py, a file Python automatically imports at interpreter startup. The agents then triggered a training API endpoint to spawn a new Python process. The new process imported the payload and established a reverse shell running as root.
At the time of discovery, this path traversal vulnerability in the medical imaging application did not correspond to any assigned security advisory and was unpatched. Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses with high confidence that it was a zero-day based on the absence of any corresponding fix, issue, advisory, or prior mention in vulnerability databases for the affected open-source project.
In a later session, the attackers entered the loop once the agents had identified the zero-day and provided the agents with a proxy that tunneled into a second university network.
“The server that the proxy connected to was running the same vulnerable software, and we infer the actor had used the zero-day to compromise it and establish the tunnel,” Amazon said. “The actor directed the agents to use the tunnel to target other machines in that network.”
As Amazon noted, the speed and persistence of Cairn and other AI-assisted hacking frameworks present a new challenge to defenders.
“The operational tempo in these cases compresses the window available for defensive response,” Amazon said. “An agent that discovers and exploits a zero-day in minutes completes its activity faster than many security operations centers can manually triage an alert.”

Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası ( TCMB ), kredi kartı işlemlerinde bankaların uygulayabileceği azami faiz oranlarının hesaplanmasında kullanılan referans oranı aşağı çekti. Kasım 2023'ten bu yana yüzde 3,11 seviyesinde bulunan referans oran, 1 Aralık 2026 itibarıyla yüzde 2,94 olarak uygulanacak.
Referans orandaki 0,17 puanlık düşüş, kredi kartı işlemlerinde uygulanacak azami akdi ve gecikme faiz oranlarına da yansıyacak. Böylece kredi kartı dönem borcunun tutarına göre belirlenen faiz oranları 1 Aralık'tan itibaren daha düşük seviyelerde uygulanacak.
TCMB'nin yayımladığı yeni faiz tablosuna göre, dönem borcu 30 bin TL'nin altında olan kredi kartlarında aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 3,25'ten yüzde 3,08'e inecek. Bu grupta azami gecikme faiz oranı da yüzde 3,55'ten yüzde 3,38'e düşecek.
Dönem borcu 30 bin TL ile 180 bin TL arasında olan kredi kartlarında azami akdi faiz yüzde 3,75'ten yüzde 3,58'e, azami gecikme faizi ise yüzde 4,05'ten yüzde 3,88'e gerileyecek.
Dönem borcu 180 bin TL'nin üzerinde olan kredi kartlarında ise azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 4,25'ten yüzde 4,08'e, gecikme faiz oranı yüzde 4,55'ten yüzde 4,38'e indirilecek. Bu son gruptaki oranlar, dönem borcuna bakılmaksızın kurumsal kredi kartları için de geçerli olacak.
Faiz indirimi nakit çekim ve kullanım işlemlerini de kapsıyor. Buna göre nakit avans işlemlerinde uygulanabilecek aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 4,25'ten yüzde 4,08'e, azami gecikme faiz oranı ise yüzde 4,55'ten yüzde 4,38'e düşecek.
Aynı oranlar kredili mevduat hesaplarında (KMH) da uygulanacak. Böylece hesabında yeterli bakiye bulunmadığında kredili mevduat hesabından yararlanan müşterilerin de faiz maliyeti azalacak.
Yabancı para cinsinden kredi kartı işlemlerinde de indirim yapılacak. Bu işlemlerde aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 2,98'den yüzde 2,86'ya, azami gecikme faiz oranı ise yüzde 3,28'den yüzde 3,16'ya gerileyecek.
Faiz indiriminin kredi kartı kullanıcılarına yansıması, dönem borcunun ne kadarının ödendiğine bağlı olacak. Kredi kartı borcunun tamamını son ödeme tarihine kadar kapatan kullanıcılar alışveriş borçları için faiz ödemiyor. İndirimden asıl yararlanacak kesim, dönem borcunun tamamını ödeyemediği için kalan tutarı sonraki aya devredenler olacak.
Örneğin, dönem borcundan 10 bin TL'yi sonraki aya taşıyan bir kullanıcının aylık azami akdi faiz oranı yüzde 3,25'ten yüzde 3,08'e inecek. Buna göre 10 bin TL üzerinden hesaplanan aylık faiz tutarı 325 TL'den 308 TL'ye düşecek. Böylece vergiler hariç 17 TL'lik faiz avantajı oluşacak.
Aynı hesaplamayla 50 bin TL'lik devreden borçta aylık faiz 1.875 TL'den 1.790 TL'ye, 200 bin TL'lik devreden borçta ise 8.500 TL'den 8.160 TL'ye gerileyecek. Bu hesaplamalar, borcun bir ay boyunca değişmediği varsayımıyla ve vergiler hariç yapılmıştır.
TCMB'nin ilan ettiği oranlar, bankaların kredi kartı işlemlerinde uygulayabileceği en yüksek faiz oranlarını gösteriyor. Bankalar bu sınırları aşmamak koşuluyla müşterilerine uygulayacakları faiz oranlarını serbestçe belirleyebiliyor. Dolayısıyla yeni oranlar, bütün bankaların kredi kartı faizlerini mutlaka aynı seviyeye indireceği anlamına gelmiyor.

Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to?
Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes? Then let your AI agent do it. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on their apps – and the high street.
Muse has been a hit in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, having been downloaded millions of times.
Muse can be used as an app or directly within Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform. Meta invites users to give their assistant a name, a look and a personality, so they can talk to it as well as assign it tasks such as sending an email, booking travel or buying festive presents.
“From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar … Muse can get it done for you,” said Meta.
Meta acknowledged that handing control of your day-to-day digital life to an AI agent is “an act of trust”. Muse cannot make a purchase or send an email without your permission and will only connect to apps you let it join. The app has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods, Meta said, and it does not share your conversations with advertisers. It will ask for your approval before making a purchase or sending an email, while a separate “security agent” checks Muse’s actions against the permissions you’ve granted.
“Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar,” said Meta. “To get those jobs done, you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.”
Meta said it has signed deals with an array of British businesses – including Marks & Spencer, electrical retailer Currys, Sainsbury’s and easyJet – allowing Muse to navigate their websites more easily.
In a statement last month UK regulators including the Competition and Markets Authority and the Information Commissioner’s Office said AI agents – the term for AI programmes that carry out series of tasks without human intervention – could “unlock wider innovation” but could also “amplify and accelerate risks and introduce new ones”. The watchdogs said concerns such as fraud, scams and misuse of personal information needed to be addressed by companies providing personal AI agents .
Reuters reported last week that Meta employees had raised concerns about the app’s performance, including one staff member receiving a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an encrypted messaging app. In another example reported by Reuters, Muse delivered a message with random bank account balances in it.
Meta said internal testing is vital for product development and allows the company to implement safety and privacy protection before releasing anything publicly. It is understood the majority of problems flagged by Reuters related to a bug that has been fixed.
Muse is powered by Muse Spark, Meta’s first model from the company’s “super intelligence” AI lab . In a social media post on Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, raised the possibility of humanity losing control over AI systems that are able to improve themselves autonomously.
“It is … hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with super intelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field,” he wrote.
Responding to reports that AI had cracked one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – the Riemann hypothesis – Wang said the tech industry needed to make progress in the “extremely urgent” areas of AI safety, security and alignment. Alignment refers to ensuring an AI system adheres to human goals and values.
