Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya minority
Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging that many asylum seekers in the country had been victims of “atrocities” carried ​out by the junta in Naypyidaw.
The announcement comes just days after the UN’s highest court ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
Malaysia’s prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, said on Tuesday that the deportations were in line with advice from the international court of justice (ICJ), which was “to guarantee a safe and dignified return” for those fleeing persecution, and his country had not abandoned its principles of upholding the rights of the people of Myanmar .
The UN has previously warned that migrants sent back to Myanmar could face a dangerous homecoming.
It is unclear how many Rohingya, a Muslim minority group, are among those facing deportation. However, the Rohingya make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the UN. Many of the Rohingya escaped to Malaysia during a brutal military crackdown in 2017.
Anwar acknowledged that many asylum seekers in Malaysia were “victims of atrocities carried ​out by the Myanmar regime”, but said Malaysia could ‌no longer afford to host refugees. Hoping for them to be resettled in third countries had not worked, he said.
Many in Malaysia have grown increasingly frustrated by ‌the presence of refugees in the country, saying that hosting them has become a financial burden and a security risk, with a rise in anti-migrant sentiment in the country.
On Tuesday Anwar told Malaysia’s parliament that three naval ships would return 1,500 people in December, with an additional 5,303 people flown back by aircraft at the expense of the Myanmar government.
Tuesday’s announcement follows last week’s ICJ ruling in The Hague that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ had never previously found a state responsible for genocide, and the judgment ended a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.
The 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh, arriving with reports of mass killings of adults and children, gang rapes and burnt-down villages.
In its judgment, the ICJ said Myanmar authorities must “allow and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return” of refugees displaced either within Myanmar or abroad.
In September, Malaysia began sending back a group of about 1,500 Myanmar nationals as it launched its contested repatriation plan.
Malaysia’s government said in a statement at the time that the repatriation was necessary to resolve the “legacy issue” of foreign asylum seekers in Malaysia – of which it said 95% were from Myanmar.
“This long-standing issue has imposed a significant financial burden on the nation, triggered serious social crises, and created tangible security threats for the Malaysian people,” the statement said.
The UN had urged Malaysia to stop that repatriation, saying nobody should be deported to Myanmar, given the severity of the situation on the ground.
In late October, the Malaysian government said it would seek clarification from Myanmar over reports that hundreds of migrants recently returned were being held in military detention.

The Best espresso machines for home must thread a delicate needle. Espresso is forceful and finicky, and a little intimidating, and yet so essential that astronauts might take it into orbit . A home espresso machine remains the most intense and expensive device I regularly operate before my first cup of coffee.
I tend to favor devices that let technology do much of the work and don’t make you join a cult of engineers before your first cup. And so my top-rated espresso machine, the Fellow Series 1 , earned its place on WIRED’s counter by combining ease of use with a solid build, consistent temperature, and rare control over pressure—an industry-beating mix of nerdiness and hand-holding friendliness. For a more classic, all-analog build, we offer the compact, stylish Diletta Mio .
But I know not everyone wants to also buy a good coffee grinder or spend four figures for their morning cup. For those who want milk-based drinks and a built-in grinder, I recommend the top-selling Breville Barista Express as the Goldilocks machine balancing performance and cost. For an entry-level device, I pretty much always recommend the straight-ahead Breville Bambino , among the lowest-cost machines with PID-controlled temperature.
Note that this guide mostly covers classic, hands-on espresso machines with portafilters. We do also include the De'Longhi Rivelia , our top pick among super-automatic espresso machines that require little more than a button press. For a guide that focuses on easy-to-use espresso machine picks that do most of the work for you, check out our guide to the Best Latte and Automatic Espresso Machines .
Also, be sure to check out our other coffee guides, like the Best Drip Coffee Makers, Best Cold Brew Makers , Best Aeropresses , Best Coffee Pod Machines , Best Coffee Subscriptions , and Best Coffee Grinders .
Updated November 2026: We’ve added information on Meraki’s second-run release and ensured up-to-date links and prices.
San Francisco-based Fellow is almost certainly the most innovative and tech-forward coffee machine company of the moment. And rarely has an espresso machine so swiftly changed what I want from the best espresso makers as the Fellow Series 1 , which started shipping in early 2026. Sure, the temperature control is admirable, with a patented heating technology that threads the needle between the fast heating of a thermoblock and the stability of a boiler. Automatic milk frothing is about as good and as fast as it gets. The dial and LED-screen controls are intuitive. And the device is compact, conserving both counter space and airspace.
But the real game-changing addition with this machine is the way Fellow has introduced tight pressure control and shot profiles to the non-geek home espresso landscape. Almost every other espresso machine on the market just sorta aims at 9 bars of pressure and shrugs. The Series 1 offers profiles for light, medium, or dark roast that change pressure based on what's right for each bean—keeping dark roasts classic but pulling longer shots and dialing back pressure on light-roast beans. Other profiles, like turbo shots or “Modern Arc,” cater to the modern yen for espresso with less bitterness.
After testing for weeks, I'm sold. You'd pay at least double to find this feature on any other espresso machine. And no device lets you play with pressure as easily as the Fellow, even before a planned firmware update that'll allow you to sync profiles through Fellow's phone app. The app remains mostly a placeholder for now, offering tutorials and education but TBD functionality. But Fellow's track record building out the app on my top-pick drip coffee machine , the Fellow Aiden , gives me confidence this is a temporary blip. Volumetric controls still need tweaking, and the removable water reservoir can only be removed straight up from the device, requiring significant clearance.
But even with these early quirks, the Fellow Series 1 remains the most impressive espresso machine I've tested in the past couple of years. And it's changed what I want from espresso machines in the future. The Series 1 might already be the most-hyped machine of 2026. But this time, the hype is warranted.
The Barista Express had been our top pick for years, a Goldilocks choice in terms of price, versatility, and performance. It remains among the most popular espresso machines in the world (and possibly the most popular, period) for good reason. The Barista Express produces consistent pressure for espresso, its steam wand is excellent, and the built-in grinder makes it an all-in-one device. Its mostly metal construction, easy cleaning, and other thoughtful touches make it a faithful companion. My WIRED colleague Julian Chokkattu has been using his machine happily for seven years. And its price, which drops regularly during sales events, makes it accessible to mere mortals. For those who want a built-in grinder but don't want to spend four figures, this is an easy recommendation.
Competitors have taken direct aim at the Express with impressive semiautomatic entries like the Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier ($599) and Luxe Cafe Pro (see below), plus the De'Longhi La Specialista Opera ($900) . Each of these offers more options, including cold espresso, with similar grind quality. For now, WIRED's years of testing and vetting the Barista Express, and Breville's good customer service reputation, keep the Express as my top recommendation. But in the meantime, I wouldn't be sad to see the Barista Express updated to better Baratza burrs on that built-in grinder, as Breville has done with its more expensive machines.
Upgrade pick: The Barista Express is a great mix of price and performance. But Breville's true top-line semiautomatic machine is the Breville Oracle Jet ( $1,980 on Amazon ), a touchscreen device with a better grinder that'll also offer better control and easier milk frothing and can guide you through everything from the proper bean grind to how to make a proper flat white, cappuccino, or espresso martini.
A classic espresso machine rewards effort with nuance and beauty. And the Diletta Mio is everything a classic Italian-made espresso machine should be. It's compact, stylish, built to last, and brews circles around the competition. It's also a simple joy to use, wrote former WIRED reviewer Jaina Grey. It feels a bit analog, like an heirloom-quality stand mixer , but also sports sophisticated features like a PID (proportional-integral-derivative) temperature controller—a wee processor with an algorithm that keeps brew temperatures stable. Among traditional espresso machines that require a separate grinder, this is the one WIRED recommends.
Upgrade: WIRED's upgrade pick, the Diletta Bello ($1,899) , is for advanced beanheads who love a sensitive machine. On the Bello, every difference makes a difference: every micron of grind size, or slight gradation of tamping pressure, will produce a different cup of espresso. But when you've dialed in your bean, the Bello is beautifully faithful—offering shot after shot of caramely crema and rich espresso.
The Bambino is little, fast, low-cost, and convenient—about as wide as a one-dollar bill. There are no apparent frills and no grinder: just a steam wand for silky milk and a choice between single or double shots. But look under the hood of this $300 beauty and you'll note features that are hallmarks of much more expensive machines: a thermoblock for immediate heating and a PID (proportional, integral, derivative) temperature controller that makes for consistent brew temps usually out of reach at this price range.
Which is to say it's a wee machine that pulls far above its weight class. Pair your Bambino with a good mid-level grinder and you'll be making beautiful cups with counter space to spare, for a total of $500.
Upgrade: The Breville Bambino Plus ($500) is hardier and slightly bigger and offers automatic milk frothing.

The Pakistan Air Force pilot will spend about a week on board the Tiangong, conducting experiments with China’s crew.
Islamabad, Pakistan – Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when an air force pilot joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, will fly as a payload specialist alongside commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 8:18am Beijing time (00:18 GMT), or 5:18am in Pakistan.
Speaking at a news conference in Jiuquan on Tuesday, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said the mission would mark the first joint flight by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the country’s crewed space programme.
After reaching orbit, the spacecraft will carry out a rapid, autonomous rendezvous lasting about three and a half hours before docking with the forward port of the station’s Tianhe core module, Zhang said.
Ali’s stay will be brief. He will return to Earth on board the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after a short joint flight, while Zhu Yangzhu, a member of that crew, remains in orbit for a year, Zhang said.
Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) has said Ali will spend about a week on the station.
“I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis,” Ali told reporters during the crew’s conversation with the media.
Ali and Khurram Daud, a second Pakistani selected for astronaut training, are Pakistan Air Force pilots.
They were selected through a three-stage process that began with screening in Pakistan and included medical, psychological and technical assessments.
CMSA named them reserve astronauts on April 22 earlier this year. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met them in Islamabad the following day, and on April 24, China’s Space Day, they joined the Astronaut Center of China in Beijing for training.
Before leaving, Daud asked Pakistanis to pray for him in a video released by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
“My message to you all is to pray for me, so that I can complete this training and this mission well, and make my nation and my country proud,” he said in Urdu.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China for the launch, paid tribute to both men on X on Tuesday.
“They trained in centrifuges and simulators, in emergency drills and in a new language. Both performed exceptionally well in training. Though Zeeshan Ali will fly tomorrow both have already made Pakistan proud,” he wrote.
Thanking his instructors, SUPARCO and CMSA, at Tuesday’s news conference, Ali said: “No matter who flies, we have already made the history together.”
Daud was not named in the crew, and it is not yet clear whether he will fly on a later mission.
In written responses to Al Jazeera, SUPARCO said the backup astronauts would serve as experts to help carry the programme forward.
Zhang said Ali would take part in the crew’s daily work but would mainly oversee China-Pakistan experiments, install samples and equipment and conduct tests in orbit.
The mission will include four joint science projects in biotechnology and materials, Zhang said. Ali will also conduct an experiment involving cyanobacteria, photosynthetic microorganisms.
Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the experiments would cover materials science, fluid physics, life sciences and biotechnology, with potential applications in climate resilience, food security and industrial innovation.
Qamarul Islam, a space scientist and former senior official in the state-affiliated Institute of Space Technology (IST) in Islamabad, said the experiments had been shortlisted after SUPARCO invited research institutes in Pakistan to submit proposals.
“Primarily these experiments are the experiments of the research institutes, universities and others, from Pakistan,” he told Al Jazeera.
SUPARCO said the station was a fully equipped laboratory. It added in its response that Ali’s week in orbit was meant to start and install the experiments, and to record data confirming that the equipment had survived launch loads and vibrations and was safely installed in microgravity.
“Completing the four experiments takes between six and 12 months,” it said.
According to Zhang, preparations focused on professional skills, crew coordination and language.
“We focus on Chinese commands and technical terms to ensure accurate execution,” he said, in the English interpretation of his remarks.
In a promotional video by the Chinese space agency, Ali, who described himself as a fighter pilot, said centrifuge, rescue and survival, and emergency procedures training were part of his preparation.
“But the real challenge, honestly speaking, was mastering the Chinese language, because all the switches, all the software, all the programmes, all the voice announcements, everything is in Chinese. So we had to learn that and master that technical Chinese,” he said.
SUPARCO and CMSA signed their astronaut agreement in Islamabad in February 2025. Ali said the two countries had since moved quickly.
“The two great nations of China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time,” he said.
This year marks 75 years of diplomatic ties between the two neighbours. Zhang described the flight as another milestone in their cooperation.
“Pakistan is China’s all-weather strategic cooperative partner,” Zhang said, according to the English interpretation of his remarks.
Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the programme placed the country among a select group of nations involved in human spaceflight.
China built its own space station after being excluded from the International Space Station (ISS), in part because a 2011 US law bars NASA from bilateral cooperation with Beijing.
“Chinese were left out. And obviously China developed their own space station. Pakistan is also out of the International Space Station as far as the astronauts are concerned,” Qamar said.
He said China’s decision to choose Pakistan for its first foreign visitor reflected the two countries’ closeness.
Asked by a reporter on Tuesday whether China would expand cooperation, including joint flights with Russia, Zhang pointed to the station’s transport and astronaut-training systems. He said China hoped to explore space with more countries and regions.
SUPARCO said Pakistan was opening a path for international collaboration on the Chinese station and could now offer its expertise to other countries.
Asked by China’s state-run CGTN about the future of the partnership, Ali looked beyond the current mission.
“I believe what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself. This mission is not a finish line; it is a launchpad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation to grow from one astronaut, one flight, to multiple joint flights, to Moon, Mars, and beyond.”
Asked about lunar plans, SUPARCO said Pakistan was already working with China on a lunar mission tentatively planned for 2028. It said it could not yet disclose details.
Pakistan’s lunar programme has so far focused on robotic missions. The iCube-Qamar satellite, developed at IST, reached the lunar orbit on board China’s Chang’e-6 mission in 2024. A SUPARCO-developed rover is due to fly on the Chang’e-8 about 2028.
Qamar, who was the project director for iCube-Qamar, said lunar missions ranged from flybys and orbiters, such as the satellite, to landings and eventually permanent bases.
“In the long term you will see stations on the Moon, a utilisation of the Moon,” he said.
China is also advancing its lunar programme. Zhang said preparations were under way for tests of the Long March-10 rocket and Mengzhou crewed spacecraft. The first flight of the Lanyue lunar lander was on track, he said. Beijing aims to put astronauts on th…

The free, open source PhoneBox dashboard puts old Android screens back to work.
My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don’t meet your daily driving needs. It’s tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you’re holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren’t hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use.
I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in “the drawer.”
Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn’t have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you’d like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.
I already had developer mode initialized on the tablet but had to go back and allow ADB over USB in settings. The total installation time from copying the script from the project website to everything running on my PC and tablet was less than a minute. The app is MIT-licensed , works on Android 5.0 or later, and requires sideloading, since it is not available on the Google Play Store .
The installation script also prints its own uninstall script before it finishes. So often these days, getting rid of an unwanted app feels more difficult than installing it, so I appreciate the straightforward approach the developer has implemented.
The first time you fire up PhoneBox, you get live performance and diagnostic information from your PC, along with several pages of optional content that can be tweaked for your local setup to display information that’s pertinent to your uses.
Where PhoneBox really starts to shine is the widget catalog—a collection of free add-ons that can be added as pages to the tablet’s cycling page layouts. There are more general widgets, such as RSS feeds that display news highlights from your chosen sources, or simple displays like timers or world clocks.
I opted for a few different widgets that caught my eye. One let me view my library of installed Steam titles and launch them on my PC with a simple tap of the tablet screen. Another allows me to control smart home entities hosted by my Home Assistant server. I was controlling the lights in my office from my tablet within seconds of adding the widget. It’s brilliant.
Setting up additional widgets is as simple as adding them to the page layout from the PC’s web interface and hitting save. As soon as I updated things from the PC, the connected tablet immediately began reflecting the changes. I haven’t had the chance to test most of the 131 current options in the widget catalog, but the ones I did try were simple to modify and worked on the first try.
While I didn’t have any major issues with PhoneBox, I did notice a couple of early annoyances along the way. Windows users should be aware that the PC companion app on that OS is currently unsigned, and they should expect a SmartScreen notification when attempting to install the software.
All control settings live in the web interface rather than the phone or tablet you’re connecting. When I first started messing with PhoneBox, I noticed it displayed my weather location as Tallinn. Nothing against the capital of Estonia, but that’s not weather information that does me much good here in the US Midwest. When I went into the widget settings to change the report location, there was nothing to be found. It turns out that you have to change those settings from the general user preferences section rather than within the widget itself. Not a deal-breaker by any means, but a slight hiccup for someone who was new to the software.
Connecting the Android tablet with my PC over USB was totally painless, but I never got the wireless route to work in my testing. Users are meant to generate a QR code from the PhoneBox web interface on their PC and connect it to their device by scanning the code with their phone/tablet. Every time I tried to scan the code from my device’s camera app, the tablet refused. There’s no QR scanner built into the PhoneBox app, so if your camera app won’t cooperate, the documented path dead-ends. USB was my intended route anyway and works great, but if you’re planning a wireless-only setup, be prepared for possible friction. The documented flow needs your device camera to open the pairing link, and mine wasn’t in the mood.
These minor gripes should be smoothed over before the release of 1.0. The project is early, but it seems to be moving quickly. I tested and installed PhoneBox version 0.9.29, which was one of several releases pushed to the project’s GitHub in as many days. One item of history worth noting: On November 20, the project published a high-severity security advisory covering versions 0.9.23 and earlier. The vulnerability potentially allowed another app running on the connected Android device to execute commands or receive stored credentials from the host PC. The flaw no longer existed by the time I tested the package in version 0.9.29, but it’s a good reminder that you’re installing something with deep system access and should exercise appropriate caution.
As long as you’re part of the group that has an old phone or tablet lying around somewhere, and these days I expect that most of us are, then it’s an emphatic yes. Repurposing old devices to find new lives is one of the things that keeps me a tech hobbyist. I love finding genuinely useful and practical applications for devices that have been pushed aside by their manufacturers in favor of the latest and greatest in the lineup.
PhoneBox took a tablet that was forgotten in a junk drawer and destined for donation and gave it a new lease on life. I haven’t spent a single penny, but I now have a useful secondary display on my desk. The tablet is powered via a dedicated USB port on my PC, and only goes to sleep when my main monitor displays do. Go dig through those mystery drawers in your house, because this one is worthwhile.

At least 10 wounded after blast at restaurant in the Dong Da district in Hanoi as rescue operations under way.
An explosion in a crowded residential part of Vietnam’s capital Hanoi has killed at least six people and injured 10, according to local authorities.
The blast occurred at a restaurant in the Dong Da district at about 8am (01:00 GMT) Tuesday, shattering windows, tearing metal shutters from their frames and heavily damaging surrounding buildings and homes, according to local media reports.
The restaurant was full of people at the time of the explosion, which the Ministry of Public Security believes was related to cooking gas. More people are feared to be trapped under the rubble, which rescuers have spent hours searching through, reported Vietnam’s VnExpress newspaper.
“There was a flash of light, and doors, glass and everything around me were sent flying,” the unnamed resident told the state-affiliated VietNamNet newspaper.
Photos published by VnExpress showed the restaurant, located on the ground floor of an apartment block, almost completely collapsed. Rubble was scattered across the narrow street outside, where several cars and motorbikes were damaged or overturned.
Dozens of firefighters and other rescue officials were dispatched to the scene. They were still digging through rubble more than four hours later, said VnExpress, adding that the city’s mayor was also present.
Authorities have since evacuated people from nearby buildings deemed structurally unsafe, said the report.

Çin merkezli yapay zeka şirketi Z.a i, yeni amiral gemisi yapay zeka modeli GLM-5.4'ü tanıttı . Şirketin Loop Transformer mimarisini kullanan ilk amiral gemisi modeli olan GLM-5.4, daha fazla parametre eklemeden yapay zekanın akıl yürütme kapasitesini geliştirmeyi hedefliyor.
Yeni model, yazılım geliştirmenin yanı sıra video üretimi, oyun tasarımı ve 3D modelleme gibi alanlarda da kullanılabiliyor. Yaklaşık 750 milyar parametre ölçeğinde geliştirilen GLM-5.4, mevcut GLM-5 modelinin 28 katmanını iki kez çalıştırıyor. Geleneksel Transformer modellerinde her katman bir kez işlenirken yeni mimari, aynı katmanları tekrar kullanarak daha kapsamlı akıl yürütme yapılmasına olanak tanıyor. Böylece modelin parametre sayısı artırılmadan işlem kapasitesinden daha fazla yararlanılması amaçlanıyor.
Z.ai, bu yöntem sayesinde GLM-5.4'ün 2 ila 3 trilyon parametreye sahip modellerle karşılaştırılabilir bir performans seviyesine ulaştığını öne sürüyor. Ancak şirketin bu iddiasını destekleyen, GLM-5.4'e ait kapsamlı ve bağımsız olarak doğrulanmış performans testleri henüz yayımlanmadı.
Z.ai, yeni modelle birlikte Generalized Coding olarak adlandırdığı yaklaşımı da öne çıkarıyor. Bu yaklaşım, kodlamanın yalnızca yazılım geliştirmek için değil, farklı alanlardaki karmaşık görevleri gerçekleştirmek için de kullanılmasına dayanıyor.
Şirketin paylaştığı örneklerde GLM-5.4'ün kendi anlatımını oluşturduğu bir müzik videosu hazırladığı, FreeCAD kullanarak altı eksenli bir robot kolu modellediği ve fizik mekanikleri, haritalar ve savaş sistemi içeren bir oyun geliştirdiği görülüyor. Model ayrıca özel GLSL gölgelendiricileri kullanarak etkileşimli 3D ortamlar oluşturabiliyor.
GLM-5.4'ün görsel içerikleri işleme yetenekleri de geliştirilmiş durumda. Böylece model, yalnızca metin tabanlı komutlarla değil, görsel girdilerden yararlanarak da kodlama ve tasarım görevlerini yerine getirebiliyor. İlk testlerde dikkat çeken sonuçlar Z.ai, Loop Transformer mimarisini 1 milyar, 4 milyar, 30 milyar ve 750 milyar parametre ölçeğindeki modeller üzerinde test etti.
Şirketin paylaştığı sonuçlara göre yeni mimari, 30 milyar parametreli bir model üzerinde yapılan testlerde, eğitim sırasında yaklaşık yüzde 10 daha fazla işlem gücü kullanarak matematik, bilimsel akıl yürütme ve uzun metinleri anlama gibi alanlarda daha başarılı sonuçlar elde etti.
Aynı testlerde MMLU-Pro yanıtlarının ortalama uzunluğu yaklaşık yüzde 15, GPQA-Diamond yanıtlarının uzunluğu ise yaklaşık yüzde 12 azaldı. Ancak bu sonuçların doğrudan GLM-5.4 üzerinde değil, mimariyi değerlendirmek amacıyla kullanılan daha küçük bir modelde elde edildiğini belirtelim. Z.ai ayrıca GLM-5.4'ün zaman zaman gereğinden uzun akıl yürütme süreçlerine girebildiğini de kabul ediyor.
GLM-5.4, GLM Coding Plan abonelerinin tamamına sunuldu. Model, ZCode ve Z.ai Chat üzerinden de kullanılabiliyor. Haftalık kullanım kotasına sahip abonelere ise GLM-5.3'e kıyasla yüzde 50 daha fazla kullanım hakkı tanınıyor. Z.ai'nin paylaştığı bilgilere göre model, yoğun olmayan saatlerde saniyede 200 token'a kadar çıktı üretebiliyor. Yoğun kullanım saatlerinde ise bu hız saniyede 70 ila 80 token seviyesinde oluyor.
GLM-5.4'ün API erişiminin güvenlik değerlendirmelerinin tamamlanmasının ardından açılması planlanıyor. Şirket, modelin ağırlıklarını da gerekli güvenlik çalışmalarını tamamladıktan sonra paylaşacağını belirtiyor.

Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.
In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.
"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.
In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest.
Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign .
"Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry.
"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious."
Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he said he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes.
"He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he said happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires.
He said the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome.
"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".
The collection of diaries was edited by a longtime friend of Francis
The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".
"I watched a little, and it terrified me," he said, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".
"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.
Cardinal Victor Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and friend of Francis, edited the diaries, which are the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s.
Pope Francis was elected pope in 2013 and died aged 88 in April 2025.

Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.
The first foreign astronaut on a Chinese space mission said on Tuesday that he will be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" when the latest crew blasts off on Wednesday.
Beijing has poured billions into the Chinese space programme, whose prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts that are typically rotated every six months.
The Shenzhou-24 mission is set to lift off at 8:18am (0018 GMT) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan launch centre in China's northwestern Gobi Desert, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesman Zhang Jingbo told a news conference on Tuesday.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani payload specialist, will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station.
"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a separate news conference held later to introduce the crew.
"To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he said in English, following other remarks in fluent Mandarin and Urdu.
Ali will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong in May.
Pakistani officials welcomed Ali's selection as a significant step in relations between Islamabad and Beijing.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a "source of joy and pride for the entire nation".
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission underscored the trust and "iron brotherhood" between the two countries.
Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar explorer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.
Beijing has invested heavily in its space programme in recent years, seeking to catch up with its principal rival , the United States.
Pakistan, which maintains close diplomatic and trade ties with Beijing, is a natural partner in the endeavour.
The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40.
Lai is Hong Kong 's first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard the space station.
Watch more Conquering the far side of the Moon: Breaking down China's historic lunar mission
After the new, all-male crew reaches the Tiangong, Pakistan's Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.
Zhu will remain on board to complete China's first full-year stay in space – a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.
Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space.
Tang told reporters that learning to work together was more challenging in this mission, pointing to differences in language, culture and even psychology. But efforts from both sides have been paying off, Tang said.
“The labels and operating instructions aboard the spacecraft and space station are all in Chinese, and the Pakistani astronaut began training with virtually no foundation of the language," he said, adding that he and Wu also stepped up their English learning.
The Long March-2F rocket that will carry the crew into space will soon be filled with propellant, the CMSA's Zhang said.
The crew is in good condition and the space station is functioning normally, meeting all requirements for the mission, he said.

Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously".
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the reports but dismissed stories citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutscher Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Asked about the reports, the Nato secretary general told a press conference in Berlin alongside Merz: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
The Western defensive alliance had a variety of response options, said Rutte.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary."
Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".
German government spokesman Stefan Kornelius warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".
Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, told the Handeslblatt newspaper that having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario".
Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit.
Bleddyn Bowen, co-director of the Space Research Centre at Durham University, said that exploding a nuclear weapon in space would have "massive infrastructural effects" as there were now more than 15,000 active satellites. But he told the BBC's Today programme that "the effect of these weapons would be extremely indiscriminate and also take out a lot of Russia's own space infrastructure".
Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
In 2024 the US accused Russia of developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation .
"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.
In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".

Saurav Das said that he was supposed to deliver a series of lectures in the UK
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.
Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".
It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.
Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests , said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.
He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.
"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," Das wrote on X.
A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.
On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".
Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.
"The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country," she wrote.
Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.
In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .
In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands of people detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.
The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.
There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.
In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.
In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport is expected to rule on Tuesday on Senegal’s appeal to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations title, 10 months after a chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal won the match in January but was stripped of the title in March, when it was awarded to Morocco.
Ten months after the Africa Cup of Nations final was chaotically played on the field between Morocco and Senegal , the title will be awarded Tuesday by sports’ highest court.
The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the target Monday to publish the verdict of its panel of three judges on Senegal’s appeal to regain the title the team won on the field in Morocco in January and then lost in a legal case in March.
A strict reading of The Laws of The Game, soccer’s ultimate rule book, should see Senegal win the case.
A broader interpretation of AFCON tournament rules would give the victory to Morocco .
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
Read more AFCON 2025: CAS set to hand down ruling on controversial final
Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. Senegal’s team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.
Match referee Jean-Jacques Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco’s penalty by Brahim Diaz was saved and Senegal won with the only goal in extra time.
CAF appeal judges later cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”.
The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.
CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland’s supreme court though only on limited procedural grounds.
The next AFCON tournament starts in June co-hosted by Kenya , Uganda , and Tanzania .

Benefit claims made easier in first stage of shake-up of welfare system
Disabled people with severe and lifelong conditions will be able to claim disability benefits more easily after a major review of the system by ministers.
The Department for Work and Pensions said on Tuesday it would immediately commit to speeding up the personal independence payment (Pip) system for adults in England and Wales who have severe conditions or ones that are unlikely to change.
Ministers are working on a broader response, however, which the Guardian understands is likely to include cuts to cash payments for those who do not meet the threshold for the new fast-track system.
The proposals will be included in a white paper to be published next year as the first step in what is likely to be the biggest shake-up of the welfare system in over a decade.
Stephen Timms, the minister for social security and disability who led the review, said: “The Timms review’s interim report was clear that while Pip is valued, the system is no longer fit for purpose.
“That’s why the government is today accepting two of its key recommendations: reducing unnecessary award reviews for people whose health conditions are lifelong, progressive or unlikely to improve, and introducing a fast-track route for people with severe, well-evidenced conditions and those nearing the end of life.
“These changes are a first step to building a system which gives greater security for those with the most severe conditions.”
The recommendations were broadly welcomed by campaigners and disability charities who said the report, drawn up in consultation with disabled people, provided the basis for a potentially fairer and more compassionate system.
But there is widespread nervousness that some claimants will fail to qualify for cash payments under a new “impact assessment” of needs. Campaigners will seek assurances that vulnerable people are not left without a financial lifeline.
Alexa Knight of the Mental Health Foundation said: “No one receiving Pip should be pushed into deeper poverty as a result of these changes, even in the short term. The consequences for individuals and their families can be devastating if support is removed before suitable alternatives are in place.”
Timms began his review last year after Keir Starmer’s government dropped a plan to cut the Pip system by £5bn in the face of a backlash from backbench MPs.
Timms defended those proposed cuts as a minister at the time, warning that without spending reductions the welfare bill would become unsustainable. The Office for Budget Responsibility has forecast that without changes, spending on Pips will rise from around £16bn in 2019-20 to just over £41bn by the end of the decade.
His final report, which was written with disability rights advocates Sharon Brennan and Clenton Farquharson, does not identify any specific areas where the overall bill could be cut.
Instead, Timms makes a series of recommendations to make the system easier to use for people with serious conditions and more tailored for those with less severe needs.
The report recommends a fast-track route for people with what Timms calls “severe, well-evidenced conditions”. It also proposes reducing the number of reviews for those with lifelong or degenerative conditions and making sure these reviews look only at what has changed rather than starting from scratch.
For others, the report calls for the system to be changed so that it better suits their needs, rather than paying out the current set rates of up to £194.60 a week.
Those who are not being fast tracked will undergo an assessment on how their condition affects their daily life to decide what cash payment they should receive. The government should spend more on face-to-face assessments, the report recommends.
The Department for Work and Pensions said the new system would “help disabled people achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence”.
Timms insists that cash payments should remain at the heart of the system, unlike Alan Milburn, who recommended in a separate report on youth joblessness that under-25s should no longer be able to claim Pip. Milburn recommended the money saved should be spent instead on schemes to help young people get into the workplace.
Ministers are now working on a formal government response, which is expected next month before a white paper in the spring.
If they follow the proposals made by Milburn and Timms, it will lead to two separate welfare systems where those aged 25 and over can claim disability benefits but younger adults cannot.
Timms’ report does leave space, however, for ministers to save money from Pip by reducing cash payments to many of those who claim it.
The Guardian has been told that ministers are working on a Pip system that would apply the Milburn model of extra work and training support combined with cash cuts for all ages who do not meet the threshold for the new fast-track system.

Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying
A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.
Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May . Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.
The incident comes a month after he was detained for defying a security crackdown in Delhi during protests demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner.
“This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), Edinburgh to deliver talks on the Cockroach movement,” Das said in a social media post late on Monday. “Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual government was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions.”
Das was due to speak at the Oxford Union society on 1 December.
CJP-organised protests in July over alleged examination irregularities forced the education minister to resign , marking a rare climbdown by the government of Narendra Modi.
Critics say human rights and press freedoms have declined since Modi came to power in 2014. Earlier this month, India barred more than 100 foreign speakers from attending a democracy summit organised by the opposition Congress party. Those denied visas included a Norwegian journalist who had previously questioned Modi about press freedom.
In 2022, authorities prevented Sanna Irshad Mattoo, an award-winning photographer from India-administered Kashmir, from flying to the US to collect her Pulitzer prize.

A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.
Over the summer, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that he expected between 30,000 and 50,000 North Korean soldiers would be deployed to Russia as part of Pyongyang's ongoing support of Moscow's war effort .
However, it now appears that troop buildup has yet to materialize, and it is unclear whether North Korea will continue sending large numbers of troops to Russia.
Writing on Telegram on November 9, Andrii Kovalenko, who resigned in September as head of Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation, said an August intelligence assessment indicated that the Kremlin had requested more than 30,000 additional North Korean troops for an autumn offensive.
He said a summit between North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Russian President Vladimir Putin was expected in September, but did not happen. Kviy has claimed that North Korea previously sent thousands of troops to Russia's Kursk region in 2024, where Moscow was fighting to repel a Ukrainian incursion.
Kovalenko believes Pyongyang turned down Moscow's request because taking part in offensive operations in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine's Donetsk region may still be a red line for North Korea .
However, Kovalenko added that Russia still relies on North Korean material support, particularly ammunition, while assessing that another major deployment of North Korean combat troops was unlikely this winter.
Han Ki-bum, a former deputy director of South Korea's National Intelligence Service, told DW that the lull in fighting and the onset of winter give Pyongyang little immediate reason to send reinforcements.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
He added that a visit this week to Moscow by Jo Yong-won, a senior North Korean official and close aide to Kim, could shed light on any future plans.
Han said it remained to be seen whether the visit was intended to deepen political ties between the ruling parties, building on their military cooperation, or to lay the groundwork for a visit by Kim himself.
Ahn Chan-il, a former North Korean soldier who defected to South Korea in 1979 and now heads the World Institute for North Korea Studies in Seoul, said Moscow also had reasons to limit the deployment.
He told DW that he expects Russia to weigh its battlefield needs against the costs of bringing in more North Korean troops. Unless the war expands, he said, Moscow is unlikely to request a larger contingent.
Ukrainian official Kovalenko said North Korea still had a missile unit in Russia's Voronezh region and around 8,500 support personnel in rear areas, including drone operators, engineers and sappers.
He added that Pyongyang was ramping up ammunition production and showcasing new drones and missiles.
In a post on X on November 17, Zelenskyy said that Russia was receiving dozens of North Korean ballistic missiles each month.
He warned that their use in Ukraine was helping Pyongyang refine its weapons and creating security risks for countries around the Korean Peninsula. Battle-testing weaponry is one of North Korea's primary advantages from military cooperation with Russia
Kovalenko said Pyongyang appeared to have adopted what he called a "containment strategy," limiting its military commitment to Russia's war while maintaining ties with both Moscow and Beijing.
In his assessment, this approach allows Pyongyang to retain the benefits of its alliance with Russia while reducing its exposure to the outcome of the war.
Analyst Ahn said he expects Pyongyang's military cooperation with Moscow to continue because Russian assistance is crucial to North Korea's efforts to develop drone technology and strengthen its navy.
Nevertheless, the extent of this cooperation may be more limited in the future, and Pyongyang is also able to turn to China as a hedge.
Ahn said that if Russia limits the deployment of North Korean troops, Pyongyang's foreign currency earnings from those deployments would have less room to grow, giving it another reason to seek more support from Beijing
Jeong Joon Hee, a former South Korean Unification Ministry spokesperson, told DW that recent moves towards building better ties with Beijing may also reflect Pyongyang's dissatisfaction with what Moscow has offered in return for North Korea's help.
By strengthening its relationship with China while keeping ties with Russia steady, he said, Pyongyang could also be trying to persuade Moscow to give it more.
Kim Hyung Suk, a former South Korean vice minister of unification, told DW that North Korea needs China's economic, political and diplomatic backing alongside the support it receives from Russia. He expects Pyongyang to keep pursuing China's support regardless of how it manages its role in the war.

texts.https://www.theguardian.com/politics/liv:
In the Commons, Stephen Timms is now delivering his statement on Pip.
He says Pip provides “ vital support to deaf and disabled people and people with long term health conditions”. It was introduced 13 years ago, but has not been reviewed since then.
He says it was co-produced by himself, his two co-chair and 12 other members of a steering group. Almost all of those 12 people had “lived experience of disability or long term ill health”. Every member – including Timms himself – had just one vote, he says.
double quotation mark The review is clear that Pip remains a vital source of support, but it finds that the system is failing in three fundamental respects.
First of all, the assessment is not fit for purpose. It doesn’t consider people’s needs, their aspirations, their barriers, or their extra costs. It’s just about what somebody cannot do. Many people find it adversarial and dehumanising. It struggles to reflect fluctuating and cumulative conditions properly, and it too often leaves people fearing that work, health, treatment or greater independence will count against them. Far from supporting independence, it can be a barrier to it.
Second, awards do not consistently enable the right contribution toward the additional costs that people face. The areas of extra cost survey reviewed by the steering group showed that Pip does not always target the highest levels of support on those with the most severe needs. The future system should make the basis for support clearer, with decisions reflecting individual circumstances better.
And third, the system’s offers offers too little scope for personalised solutions. The review recommends that cash should remain central, but that people should have the choice to access practical services as part of the overall support that they receive. That would allow the system to respond more flexibly to individual needs.
double quotation mark Support should correspond more closely to genuine additional costs and needs. Cumulative and fluctuating impacts should be recognised properly, and the highest support should reflect the most severe needs. A good deal of further work is needed. The government will now undertake this work and set out its plans in next year’s white paper.
The report includes multiple recommendations. Timms says the government will consider them in full.
But the government can announce it is confirming two of them, he says.
double quotation mark First, the people with serious well evidence conditions whose effects on daily life are clear should have access to a fast-track route without an unnecessary full assessment. That should include a distinct and rapid route for people at the end of life, as at present. But others should benefit from a fast-track as well.
And second, that people whose health conditions are lifelong or degenerative, where there’s clear evidence that their functional needs are unlikely to improve, should not face repeated award reviews.
Timms says his review concluded “full system reform” was needed.
double quotation mark The review reaches the view that we need a full system reform, not just some adjustment of the forms or descriptors.
It doesn’t prescribe a final set of eligibility rules because it recognises that decisions about eligibility criteria should sit with the elected government accountable to this house.
But it does suggest principles on which those decisions should be made.
But the Green party has welcomed the Timms review. This is from the Green MP Siân Berry.
double quotation mark The long-awaited Timms review has clearly found the current situation to be dehumanising, harmful and counterproductive. And I agree the whole system should be made more responsive, specific and dependable to support equality and respect disabled people’s human rights.
The rhetoric of insult and blame must end. It is so important for the government to recognise Pip is not an out of work benefit, to be chopped away and replaced by work support and that there should be no arbitrary age discrimination. I urge Stephen Timms to remind Alan Milburn of this.
Helen Whately , the shadow work and pensions secretary, has described the Timms review as “a complete farce”. In a response, she said:
double quotation mark This review is a complete farce. After Labour abandoned welfare reform last year, all that is left is a review which will mean more spending, fewer checks, and a complete absence of substance.
Labour’s flagship review into sickness benefits has failed. Labour will never cut welfare because they are the welfare party, and their leftwing backbenchers will never let them.
The Conservatives will review the entire Pip system, remove eligibility for low-level mental health Pip claims, rapidly assess hundreds of thousands of additional claims and get Britain working again.
Here is the Department for Work and Pensions ’ news release about the Timms report.
In the Commons, Stephen Timms was due to start his statement on the reform of Pip (the personal independence payment) at 1.30pm. But the urgent question on Capita and civil service pensions has overrun – mostly because many MPs have constituents who are affected, and are asking questions.
But the embargo on the report has passed. Here is our story, by Kiran Stacey and Patrick Butler.
Zack Polanski , the Green party leader, has described nuclear weapons as a “stain” on Britain’s reputation, dismissing a headline suggesting he is in favour of keeping them.
He was referring to a Guardian story saying that he has welcomed a report from a Green party-friendly thinktank saying the UK should remain in Nato and maintain a nuclear deterrent, cooperating on it more closely with France. Polanski has welcomed the report as a contribution to the debate – but not as an indication that he agrees with all its recommendations (which is not what our report said).
In a thread on social media featuring a screenshot of the headline, Polanski says:
double quotation mark This isn’t true - I said I back a proper conversation about national security. But i’m glad for the chance to be clear:
Nuclear weapons are a stain on our country’s reputation, and we desperately need to seek security arrangements that don’t solely rely on the USA.
double quotation mark Look at what’s happening in the world - the old institutions and assumptions are crumbling.
In the last year the USA has launched countless strikes on Iran from bases in the UK, aided by our government.
That war’s cost innocent lives & driven up costs for households at home.

Gösterişli yaşamı ve sahne tarzıyla dikkat çeken ve kamuoyunda Kobra Murat olarak tanınan Murat Divandiler, mutluluğunu takipçileriyle paylaştı. Oğlu Yiğithan Divandiler'i evlendirmeye hazırlanan şarkıcı, kız istemeye gitti.
Oğlu evlilik yolunda ilk adımı atan Kobra Murat, isteme ve nişan töreni için gelin evine gitti. Eve girmeden dua eden ve genç çift için iyi dileklerde bulunan şarkıcı, kapıyı gümüş tokmakla çaldı.
Müstakbel gelinini kanatsız melek, Allah'ın nuru, başımın tacı, prensesim diye seslenen Kobra Murat , cebinden çıkardığı bir tomar doları Melisa Karaboyacı'nın üzerine saçtı.
Kobra Murat, "Dolarlı yaşa babam, altınlara basacaksın babam, yazlıkların kışlıkların olacak. Paşa gibi kocayı kapmışsın" sözleriyle herkesi neşelendirdi.
Bu anları sosyal medya hesabından paylaşan Kobra Murat , "Herkesin evladı sevdiği insanla ömrünü paylaşsın, mutlu olsun" ifadelerini kullandı.
Kobra Murat'ın müstakbel gelini Melisa Karaboyacı'nın kolundaki altın bilezikler ve boynundaki zincir de dikkat çekti.
Öte yandan bir düğünde yaptığı kobra dansı sebebiyle Kobra lakabını aldığını anlatan Kobra Murat, her fırsatta altını çok sevdiğini söylüyor.
Zaman zaman altın kaplama detaylarıyla dikkat çeken eviyle de gündem olan şarkıcı, seneler önce katıldığı bir programda servetini şu sözlerle açıklamıştı:
“İki tane altın kasamız var. İçinde 18 kilo altın var. Karım diyor ki 'Artık altın yaptırma Murat, kasalar almıyor.' Karımın üstüne, benim üstüme paralar var, çocuklarımın üstüne paralar var. 18 tane evim, 4 tane yazlığım var. Ama hepsi alın teri.”

Gösterişli tarzı ve sahne şovlarıyla tanınan Kobra Murat, bu kez oğlunun nişan merasimiyle gündeme geldi. Oğlu Yiğithan'ın evlilik yolunda ilk adımı attığı törende ailece gelin evine giden ünlü şarkıcı, müstakbel gelini Melisa Karaboyacı'ya yaptığı dolar şovuyla sosyal medyada konuşuldu. Kapıda karşılanan Kobra Murat'ın cebinden çıkardığı dolarları gelinin üzerine saçtığı anlar kameralara yansıdı.
Nişan merasimi sırasında eline bir tomar dolar alan Kobra Murat, paraları müstakbel gelini Melisa Karaboyacı'nın üzerine savurdu. Genç kıza seslenen ünlü şarkıcı, "Dolarlı yaşa babam, altınlara basacaksın babam, yazlıkların kışlıkların olacak. Paşa gibi kocayı kapmışsın" sözleriyle davetlileri güldürdü.
Nişan görüntülerinin sosyal medyada paylaşılmasıyla birlikte Melisa Karaboyacı'nın kolundaki altın bilezikler de dikkatlerden kaçmadı.
Kobra Murat'ın nişanda yaptığı dolar şovu, daha önce katıldığı programda açıkladığı mal varlığını da yeniden gündeme getirdi. Gerçek adı Murat Divandiler olan şarkıcı, haftanın hemen her günü çalıştığını, günde 21 saat mesai yapıp yalnızca 3 saat uyuduğunu söylemişti.
Servetiyle ilgili açıklamalarıyla gündeme gelen Divandiler, iki altın kasasında 18 kilo altın bulunduğunu, kendisinin, eşinin ve çocuklarının üzerine kayıtlı paralar olduğunu, ayrıca 18 evi ve 4 yazlığı bulunduğunu açıklamıştı. Ünlü isim, tüm mal varlığını alın teriyle kazandığını vurgulamıştı.

Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığına bağlı İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi, Anadolu’nun tarihi ve kültürel zenginliğini çağdaş opera anlayışıyla Atatürk Kültür Merkezi sahnesine taşıyor.
Bestesi Güldiyar Tanrıdağlı’ya, librettosu Prof. Dr. İskender Pala’ya ait eser; Lidya Krallığı’nın son döneminde yaşanan siyasi mücadeleleri, Pers tehdidini ve insan ilişkilerini müziğin anlatım gücüyle izleyiciye aktaracak.
MÖ 6. yüzyılda ekonomik zenginliği, siyasi gücü ve başkenti Sard ile Anadolu tarihinin önemli uygarlıklarından biri olan Lidya Krallığı ’nın son dönemini konu alan eser, tarihsel olayları evrensel değerler üzerinden ele alıyor.
Bir toplumun gerçek gücünün sahip olduğu topraklardan, zenginliklerden ve siyasi iktidardan çok, kuşaktan kuşağa aktardığı kültürel miras ve değerlerde saklı olduğu düşüncesinden hareket eden opera; adalet, toplumsal düzen ve etik değerler üzerinden uygarlıkların kalıcılığını sorguluyor.
Rejisör Caner Akın tarafından sahneye konulan eser, geleneksel opera anlatımını çağdaş ve deneysel sahneleme teknikleriyle buluşturuyor.
Dekor, kostüm, ışık ve video tasarımlarıyla zenginleşen prodüksiyon, Lidya’nın tarihsel dünyasını günümüz sahnesine taşırken izleyicilere görsel ve müzikal bir deneyim sunuyor.
İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Orkestrasını İbrahim Yazıcı’nın yöneteceği prodüksiyonun dekor ve görsel tasarımını Efter Tunç, kostüm tasarımını Olcay Engin Kaymaz, ışık tasarımını Cem Yılmazer, video tasarımını Aisha Hajiyeva, koreografisini ise Berk Sarıbay üstleniyor. İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Korosu’nu Anıl Aydın hazırlıyor.
Eserde Edusa karakterini dönüşümlü olarak Gülbin Günay ve Evren Işık Yasemin canlandıracak. Halludas rolünde Mert Süngü ve Ufuk Toker, Krezüs rolünde Göktuğ Alpaşar ve Gökhan Ürben, Namirek rolünde Nesrin Gönüldağ ve Asude Karayavuz, Kyros rolünde Yoel Keşap ve Hüseyin Likos, Solon rolünde Caner Akgün ve Kevork Tavityan, Karuna rolünde Barbora Hitay ve Deniz Likos sahne alacak.
Eserin geniş sanatçı kadrosunda Berk Dalkılıç, Bülent Külekçi, Alper Göçeri, Murat Güney, Kenan Dağaşan, Emre Güngör, Burak Kul, Talip Savranbaşı, Arda Durgut, Ufuk Karakoç, Efe Doğrukul, Bahadır Özkoca, Uğur Etiler, Okan Fidan, Mehmet Tükel Acar, Fuat Kılıç Aslan ve Mehmet Eminhan Turgut’un yanı sıra İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi bale ve modern dans sanatçıları da yer alacak.
Geçtiğimiz sezon dünya prömiyeri gerçekleştirilen ve İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi repertuvarında yerini alan “Edusa”, 26 ve 28 Kasım ile 10 ve 12 Aralık 2026 tarihlerinde Atatürk Kültür Merkezi Türk Telekom Opera Salonu’nda sanatseverlerle buluşacak.

54. Uluslararası Emmy Ödülleri'nde En İyi Telenovela dalının kazananı açıklandığı anda New York 'taki salonda yaşananlar, törenden gelen görüntülerle ortaya çıktı. Dev ekrana yansıyan aday masalarındaki heyecan, kazanan dizinin adı okunur okunmaz yerini şaşkınlığa ve sevinç gösterilerine bıraktı. Türkiye'den iki dizinin yarıştığı kategoride Uzak Şehir de aday olarak yer almıştı.
Brezilya'da izlenme rekorları kıran Avenida Brasil'den uyarlanan Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet..., 11 Eylül 2024'te NOW 'da yayına girdi ve Ay Yapım imzası taşıyor. Küçük yaşta annesini kaybeden, üvey annesi Nur tarafından terk edilen Leyla'nın yıllar sonra intikam ve adalet peşinde geri dönüşünü anlatan dizinin başrollerini Cemre Baysel ile Alperen Duymaz paylaşırken, Nur karakterini Gonca Vuslateri canlandırıyor.
Türk dizilerinin Emmy'deki telenovela serüveni 2017'de Kara Sevda'nın ödülüyle başlamış, 2023 'te Yargı ve 2025'te Deha ile devam etmişti; Leyla bu listeye dördüncü isim olarak yazıldı. Ödülün açıklandığı gecenin görüntüleri de bu başarının tören salonundaki karşılığını gözler önüne seriyor.
Kazananı açıklayan sunucu sahnedeyken dev ekranın aday masalarındaki yüzlerindeki şaşkınlık kameralara yansıdı. Bir yanda heyecanla bekleyenler, bir yanda elini ağzına götürenler varken görüntü kısa sürede Leyla ekibinin masasına geçti, masadakiler ayağa kalkıp birbirine sarılarak kutlamaya başladı.
Leyla'nın kategorideki rakipleri arasında Brezilya'dan Garota do Momento ile İspanya 'dan Valle Salvaje'nin ikinci sezonu yer alıyordu. Türkiye'den ikinci aday ise Kanal D ekranlarında üçüncü sezonuna ulaşan ve Lübnan yapımı Al Hayba'dan uyarlanan Uzak Şehir 'di. Pazartesi gecesi New York 'ta yapılan törende drama dalının ödülünü Carême, komedi dalının ödülünü ise División Palermo aldı.

Uluslararası Televizyon Sanatları ve Bilimleri Akademisi tarafından ABD dışında üretilmiş yapımlara verilen 54'üncü Uluslararası Emmy Ödülleri, 23 Kasım'da dağıtıldı.
Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinden oyuncular, televizyon dünyasının tanınmış isimleri ve sektör temsilcilerinin katıldığı törenin sunuculuğunu Michael Urie yaptı.
Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinden oyuncular, televizyon dünyasının tanınmış isimleri ve sektör temsilcilerinin katıldığı törende davetliler, kırmızı halıda basın mensuplarına poz verdi. Törende Uzak Şehir dizisinin başrol oyuncuları Sinem Ünsal ve Ozan Akbaba da boy gösterdi .
Gecede 22 ülkeden 64 aday arasından 16 kategoride kazananlar açıklandı. Birleşik Krallık dokuz ödülle en çok ödülü kazanan ülke oldu.
Napolyon döneminin ünlü şefi Antonin Carême'i konu eden “Carême” dizisi, Gecede En İyi Drama dalında ödül alırken, En İyi Komedi dalında ödülü alan yapım ise "Division Palermo" oldu.
En İyi TV Filmi / Mini Dizi kategorisinde de ödülü kazanan “Prisoner 951” oldu.
Louis Theroux'nun "Louis Theroux: The Settlers" adlı belgeseli de gecede En İyi Belgesel dalında ödül aldı.
Kısa format dizi kategorisinin kazananı da “The Class of 2000” oldu.
Ay Yapım imzalı "Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet" dizisi, En İyi Telenovela kategorisinde ödüle layık görüldü. Dizi adına ödülü, yapımcı Kerem Çatay ve yönetmen Hilal Saral aldı.
Brezilya ve İspanya yapımlarını geride bırakarak ödülü Türkiye'ye kazandıran “Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet” dizisi; “Kara Sevda”, “Yargı" ve “Deha”dan sonra En İyi Telenovela dalında Emmy kazanan dördüncü Türk dizisi oldu.
Başrollerini Cemre Baysel, Alperen Duymaz ve Gonca Vuslateri'nin paylaştığı "Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet" dizisi, küçük yaşta annesini kaybeden, üvey annesi Nur tarafından terk edilen Leyla'nın yıllar sonraki dönüşünü anlatıyordu.
Törende En İyi Kadın Oyuncu ödülü “Holy Sh!t” adlı dizideki rolüyle Belçikalı oyuncu Mona Mina Leon, En İyi Erkek Oyuncu ödülünü ise "Unforgivable" filmiyle İngiliz oyuncu Bobby Schofield aldı.
En İyi Sanat Programı dalında ödülü "Der Talentierte Mr. F" adlı Alman yapımı belgesel kazandı.
Haber kategorisinde de John Sparks imzalı, Ukrayna'nın doğu cephesindeki modern drone savaşlarını konu alan “The World: 24 Hours in the Kill Zone” adlı yapım ödül aldı.
Spor Belgeseli kategorisinde de ödüle uzanan "The Philipstown Wirecar Grand Prix" oldu.
Güncel Konular kategorisinde de İngiliz yapımı “Exposure: Breaking Ranks: Inside Israel's War” ödül kazandı.
Çocuk: Animasyon kategorisinde "The Scarecrows' Wedding" ödül alırken; “Educating Yorkshire”da ikinci sezonuyla En İyi Doğaçlama Eğlence Programı oldu.

İranlı şarkıcı Parastoo Ahmadi ( 29 ) ve grubundan dört kişiye, Aralık 2024'te başörtüsüz verdikleri canlı yayın konseri nedeniyle 23 Kasım Pazartesi günü Qom'da 74'er kırbaç vuruldu. Avukatlar, cezanın iptali, hafifletilmesi ya da ertelenmesi için yaptıkları tüm başvuruların reddedildiğini açıkladı.
Tahran'a yaklaşık 140 kilometre uzaklıktaki Qom'da, Ceza Hükümlerini İnfaz Dairesi'nin üçüncü şubesinde uygulanan cezayı Ahmadi'nin avukatları duyurdu. Savunma ekibinden bir isim BBC'ye, şarkıcının yanı sıra üç müzisyenin ve yapımcısının da kırbaçlandığını söyledi. Avukat Mostafa Nili'nin aktardığına göre cezayı alanlar arasında konser organizatörü Mohsen Lashkari ile müzisyenler Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri ve Amir-Ali Pirnia de var.
Beş kişi, kırbaç cezasına ek olarak iki yıl boyunca yurt dışına çıkma ve sanatsal faaliyette bulunma yasağı da aldı. Savunma ekibi BBC'ye gönderdiği açıklamada, cezanın iptali, hafifletilmesi ya da ertelenmesi için pek çok girişimde bulunduklarını, ancak hepsinin infazı yürüten kurum tarafından reddedildiğini belirtti.
Ahmadi, Qom yakınlarındaki Dayr-ı Gaçin kervansarayında verdiği 'Kervansaray Konseri'ni 2024'ün aralık ayında kendi YouTube kanalından canlı yayınladı. Kolsuz bir elbiseyle, başörtüsü takmadan sahneye çıkan şarkıcıya Ehsan Beyraghdar (piyano), Soheil Faghih-Nasiri (gitar), Amin Taheri (davul) ve Amir-Ali Pirnia (bas) eşlik etti. Salonda izleyici yoktu. Konserde, 2022'deki Mahsa Amini protestoları sırasında da seslendirdiği vatansever şarkı 'Az Khoone Javanane Vatan' (Vatanın Gençlerinin Kanından) da yer aldı.
Konser kaydı hâlâ kanalda duruyor ve 3,3 milyondan fazla izlenmiş durumda. Kanalın 77 binden fazla abonesi var. Yayının ardından 14 Aralık 2024'te Mazandaran'da gözaltına alınan Ahmadi, tepkiler üzerine ertesi gün serbest bırakılmıştı. Şarkıcı YouTube kanalındaki açıklamasında kendisini 'sevdiklerim için şarkı söylemek isteyen bir kız' diye tanıtmış ve 'Bu, görmezden gelemeyeceğim bir hak; tutkuyla sevdiğim topraklar için şarkı söylemek' demişti.
Qom'daki bir ceza mahkemesi, Ahmadi'yi ve konserde görev alan sekiz kişiyi haziranda 'kamu ahlakını zedelemek' suçundan mahkûm etmişti. Gerekçede, sanıkların 'müstehcen ve ahlaksız içerik' ürettiği ve yayımladığı öne sürüldü. Sanıklar suçlamaları reddetti. Karar eylül ayının sonunda istinaf mahkemesinde de onandı.
İran 'da kadınların başlarını örtmesi ve bol kıyafet giymesi 1979 devriminden beri yasal zorunluluk. Kadınların kamuya açık alanlarda şarkı söylemesi de yasak . Uygulama ise tutarlı değil: AFP, özellikle Tahran'da başörtüsüz kadınların sokakta görülmesinin giderek yaygınlaştığını bildirmişti. Yetkililer yine de denetimi artırma niyetinde. Tahran Başsavcısı Ali Salehi ekim sonunda, yasayı uygulamayan kurumlara karşı 'caydırıcı tedbirler' alınacağı uyarısı yaptı. Eski Meclis Başkanı Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel ise eylülde, ' savaş koşullarının' yasanın istenen sertlikte uygulanmasını engellediğini söylemişti.
ABD merkezli İran 'da İnsan Hakları Merkezi'nin savunuculuk direktörü Bahar Ghandehari, BBC'ye yaptığı açıklamada cezanın halkı İran'ın şeriat yorumuna boyun eğmesi için korkutmayı amaçladığını söyledi. Ghandehari, 'Parastoo Ahmadi'nin istediği gibi şarkı söylediği ve giyindiği için kırbaçlanması temel haklarının açık bir ihlali ve İranlı yetkililerin kadınların özgürlüklerini bastırma kararlılığının ürkütücü bir göstergesi' ifadelerini kullandı. İran İnsan Hakları Örgütü'nden Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam ise karar haziranda açıklandığında cezayı 'insanlık dışı ve aşağılayıcı' diye nitelemişti.
Ahmadi ilk örnek değil. Şarkıcı Mehdi Yarrahi, kadınları başörtülerini çıkarmaya teşvik eden bir şarkı yayımladığı için 2023 'te gözaltına alınmıştı. Zara Esmaeili de 2024'te başörtüsüz şarkı söylediği kamera görüntüleri nedeniyle tutuklanmıştı ve şu an Fransa 'da yaşıyor.
