İzdivaç programlarının fenomen gelin adayı Hanife Gürdal, 26 Haziran 2026'da Okan Kurt'la sessiz sedasız evlenmişti. Düğün hazırlıkları sırasında ayrılan ama kısa sürede barışan çiftin son hali, Hanife'nin Uludağ tatilinden yaptığı paylaşımla ortaya çıktı. Fotoğraflara düştüğü esprili not ise pozlar kadar ilgi gördü.
Her hafta stüdyoya gelen talipleri ve kendine özgü konuşmalarıyla dikkat çeken Hanife, aradığı aşkı programlarda bir türlü bulamamıştı.
İzdivaç programlarının yayından kaldırılmasının ardından sosyal medyaya yönelen Gürdal, kısa sürede fenomen oldu. Tesettürden çıkması ve verdiği kilolarla yaşadığı değişim de uzun süre konuşuldu. Paylaşımlarındaki samimi ve esprili dili sayesinde takipçi kitlesini her geçen gün büyüttü.
Kemal Ayvaz'dan boşandıktan sonra 'Yeni hayatımın ilk gününe Hanife Gürdal olarak uyandım' diyen fenomen isim, bir süre sonra Okan Kurt'la aşk yaşamaya başladı.
Nisan ayında evlilik teklifi aldığını duyuran Gürdal, o dönem yüzüğü için 'kafam kadar pırlanta' ifadesini kullanmış, 'Ben evleniyorum, haberiniz olsun' diyerek müjdeyi vermişti. Aynı paylaşımda sevgilisine 'Çadır aramaya başla çünkü seninle çadırda da yaşarım' diye seslenmesi de gündem olmuştu.
Ancak düğün hazırlıkları sürerken çiftin yolları ayrıldı. Ayrılık uzun sürmedi; ikili barıştı ve 26 Haziran 2026'da gözlerden uzak, sade bir nikahla dünyaevine girdi.
Okan Kurt nikahın ardından eşiyle karelerini 'Can yoldaşım, eşim' notuyla paylaşırken Hanife de sosyal medyadaki adını 'Hanife Gürdal Kurt' olarak güncellemişti.
Evliliklerinin beşinci ayında soluğu Uludağ'da alan çift, birlikte verdikleri pozlarla takipçilerinin karşısına çıktı. Böylece ekranların fenomen gelin adayının evlilik hayatından son kareler de ortaya çıkmış oldu.
Fotoğraflarda mutlu görüntüler veren Hanife, paylaşımına eşi için esprili bir not da düştü: 'Benim için daha çok çalışıp, daha çok çalıştığı için stres olup dünyayı bana dar eden kocamla.'
Bu not, çiftin romantik pozları kadar ilgi gördü. Kısa sürede çok sayıda beğeni alan paylaşımın yorumlarında en çok Hanife'nin eşine yazdığı bu satırlar konuşuldu.

Hollywood yıldızı Jessica Alba'nın, 16 yıllık evliliğini bitirdiği yapımcı Cash Warren ile mal paylaşımında yeni bir karar çıktı. Los Angeles Yüksek Mahkemesi, 20 Kasım'da verdiği kararla 45 yaşındaki oyuncunun eski eşine 577 bin 481 dolar ödemesine hükmetti.
ABD basınına yansıyan mahkeme belgelerine göre para, Alba'nın HonorBar Inc. adlı şirketinin kâr paylaşım planındaki emeklilik haklarından karşılanacak. Kararda, Warren'ın bu plandan belirlenen tutarın dışında bir hak elde etmeyeceği de yer aldı.
Yeni karar, çiftin boşanma sürecindeki ilk ödemenin üzerine geldi. Alba'nın, ortak mal varlığının eşit paylaşılması için eski eşine 3 milyon dolar ödemesi daha önce kararlaştırılmıştı. Böylece oyuncunun Warren'a ödeyeceği toplam tutar 3,5 milyon doları aştı.
Habertürk'ün aktardığına göre çift evlilik öncesi sözleşme imzalamamıştı. Alba'nın kurucusu olduğu Honest Company'nin değeri 623 milyon dolar, Warren'ın çorap ve iç çamaşırı markasının değeri ise en az 100 milyon dolar olarak veriliyor.
"Fantastik Dörtlü" ve "Günah Şehri" filmleri ile "Dark Angel" dizisiyle tanınan Alba, Cash Warren ile 2008'de evlenmişti. Çift Aralık 2024'te ayrılma kararı aldı; oyuncu Şubat 2025'te "şiddetli geçimsizlik" gerekçesiyle boşanma davası açtı. Boşanma bu yıl sonuçlandı.

1996 Best Model of Turkey birincisi Güzide Duran, uzun süredir göremediğini söylediği oğlu Emir'e sonunda sarılabildi ve yaşadığı anı sosyal medya hesabından takipçileriyle paylaştı. Mart ayında Adnan Aksoy ile olaylı bir süreçten sonra boşanan Duran, paylaşımına düştüğü notta hem hasretini hem de oğluna duyduğu bağlılığı satırlara döktü. O duygu yüklü cümleler, ayrılık sürecinin çocuklarla arasına nasıl yansıdığını bir kez daha hatırlattı.
Bir dönemin tanınmış mankenlerinden Güzide Duran, 1996'da Best Model of Turkey birinciliğini kazanmış, iş insanı Adnan Aksoy ile 2007'de başlayan beraberliğini 2008'de evlilikle sürdürmüştü. Bir kız bir erkek iki çocukları olan çift, 2024'te zina, hayata kast ve evlilik birliğinin temelinden sarsılması maddeleriyle karşılıklı boşanma davası açınca magazin gündemine oturmuştu.
Bu çekişmeli süreç Duran'ın çocuklarıyla arasını da olumsuz etkilemiş, Duran çocuklarını göremediğini söyleyerek bundan eski eşi Aksoy'u sorumlu tutmuştu. Dava 30 Mart 2026'da sonuçlandı ve 18 yıllık evlilik resmen sona erdi; Duran'ın avukatı Feyza Altun , müvekkilinin lehine tazminata hükmedildiğini duyurdu. Boşanmanın ardından açıklama yapan Duran ise çocuklarına olan sevgisinin ve özleminin tarifsiz olduğunu, onlara kavuşacağı günlere inancının tam olduğunu söylemişti.
Boşanma sırasında dile getirdiği kavuşma inancı, Duran'ın son paylaşımıyla oğlu Emir söz konusu olduğunda karşılık bulmuş göründü. Duran, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda 7 Ekim 2025'ten beri hasret kaldığı kalbine bugün yeniden sarıldığını yazdı ve oğlunu kokladığını, öptüğünü, içine çektiğini ama yine de doyamadığını anlattı. 'Bir anne evladına nasıl doyar ki?' diye soran Duran, aralarına zamanın, mesafelerin ve söylenen sözlerin girdiğini kabul etti; ancak bunların hiçbirinin oğlunun kalbindeki yerini değiştiremediğini söyleyerek ondan hiç vazgeçmeyeceğini ekledi. Paylaşımda kavuşmanın nerede ve nasıl gerçekleştiği yer almadı.
Duran'ın hem boşanma süreci hem de çocuklarıyla yaşadığı mesafe, Beşiktaş Jimnastik Kulübü'nün eski başkanı Fikret Orman ile yaşadığı ilişkiyle birlikte konuşulmuştu. İkilinin Temmuz 2025'te bir Boğaziçi restoranından çıkarken görüntülenmesiyle ortaya çıkan birliktelik taraflar arasında da tartışma konusu olmuş, Duran bu ilişkinin evliliğini bitirme kararı aldıktan sonra başladığını savunurken Aksoy bunun tam tersini öne sürmüştü.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c65y:
The first ever Children's Booker Prize has announced the eight books in the running for the new £50,000 award.
Five novels, two graphic novels and an illustrated collection of short stories are on the shortlist, which is aimed at children aged eight to 12.
The authors in contention include former Children's Laureate of Ireland Eoin Colfer, who is best known for his Artemis Fowl series, and teacher and children's author Catherine Bruton.
Four children have also been announced as new judges after a UK-wide competition. Twelve-year-old Ibrahim from Hampshire was one of those picked from more than 4,000 entrants.
He told me he was called back into school for a phone call with chair of judges Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who broke the news. Ibrahim said he couldn't be happier.
"First Children's Booker Prize judge! On my CV - that's going to take me a long way… I'm too overwhelmed to even be excited."
Cottrell-Boyce told the BBC "it's really, really important that this is a prize for children's books. Having judges who are children will be proof of that… If the children don't love a book, it won't win."
Ibrahim, his fellow child judges and Cottrell-Boyce will be joined on the judging panel by Ghosts and Horrible Histories actor Lolly Adefope and Sanchita Basu De Sarkar, who owns an award-winning children's book shop in north London.
Ibrahim said he loves reading "because it's just a way to unwind yourself from the outside world. If you get stuck in a book, you're not getting your face out of there until you finish it".
He's far too professional to share which books on the list he likes best, but he told me when he was reading one of them recently: "I had to tell my mum to confiscate it because I couldn't stop reading it and I was getting a headache."
Cottrell-Boyce said he isn't concerned over whether the adult judges might dominate the decision-making.
"If - like me - you've been visiting schools as a children's writer for 20 years, it's a rare thing to meet a child who is too over-awed to express an opinion. They're usually very forthright".
Ibrahim proves that point. He told me "the adults are not going to control that meeting… 100% not!"
He's looking for "something that has different perspectives, you can see it in a different way. New characters, not just the same old sloppy characters that authors make all the time. They just make these books that just have the same plot line".
The shortlisted books are by authors and illustrators from the UK, Ireland, Australia and Italy. Cottrell-Boyce described the list as "full of surprises." Here it is:
The Worst Thing That Could Possibly Happen by Guy Bass, illustrated by David Roberts. Readers on Goodreads describe it as "super creepy" and "how horror for kids should be written."
War by Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin, illustrated by Giovanni Rigano. It's the third book in their graphic novel series and tells the story of 14-year old Kat, living under siege in an unnamed European city.
The Night I Borrowed Time by Iqbal Hussain - the British-Pakistani author and former journalist's debut Children's book weaves a story through the eyes of Zubair, a seventh son who has inherited the power of time travel and tries to fix the lives of his family.
The Rambler's Curse by Mikey Please - the fantasy-comedy by the Aardman animator, who has also illustrated the book, has been described by The Guardian as a "laugh-out-loud, shaggy-dog spiral of purposes mistook".
The Teller of Tall Tales by Liz Hyder, illustrated by Tom de Freston, was a critic's choice in The Daily Telegraph. It's about a grandmother living in a remote cabin who weaves mysterious stories for her estranged grandson.
Tadpole Summer by Catherine Bruton is about a young girl who seeks solace in nature when her brother's serious illness worsens.
Séamus Almost Famous by Jessica Scott-Whyte - this is the Irish author's second book and is illustrated by Becka Moor. Poor Séamus is on a mission to emerge from the shadows of his family - even his baby sister is an accidental internet sensation.
Hometown by Australian Shaun Tan tells the story of a girl living on a distant planet who is one day told by a visitor in a spacesuit that she is actually from somewhere very far away. A review in The Observer called it "perfect fuel for a voracious imagination".
Cottrell-Boyce told the BBC the range of subjects was "amazing".
"Children's books can be about anything, can deal with anything. But the tone has to convey hope. I can't think of a darker childhood than the one endured by Anne of Green Gables. I also can't think of a more joyous book than Anne of Green Gables."
He acknowledges the worrying statistics on reading. The National Literacy Trust's Annual Literacy Survey last year showed the percentage of children and young people who said they enjoyed reading was its lowest in 20 years. Just one in three aged eight to 18 said they enjoyed reading in their free time, down by more than a third since 2005.
"That's why we're here! To fight the fight. To make sure our children have as many opportunities as possible to discover how pleasurable, how bonding, how thrilling and enriching and fortifying it can be to slip out of the prison of the present into the infinity of the story."
He doesn't try to persuade them. "I let them live their life. I live my life".
"Put a timer on your phone, make sure it's blocked and then they'll decide to do something more productive. I might be able to convince them... because it can help you with English, your confidence, and help you build self esteem."
For him, though, the best thing about a book is when it takes him into another world. "If you try to take your head out of it, it makes you think 'oh my god what's going to happen next?'"
The winning book will be announced in February next year at the Young V&A in London. 30,000 copies of the shortlisted books will be given to children who need them most.

Televizyon sektöründe yaşanan reklam krizi, oyuncu ücretleri tartışmasını da beraberinde getirdi. Reklam gelirlerindeki düşüş nedeniyle yapım şirketlerinin oyunculardan ücretlerinde indirime gitmelerini istediği öne sürülürken, bazı isimler bu teklifi kabul ediyor, bazıları ise karşı çıkıyor. "Altı Üstü İstanbul" dizisinde rol alan İlker Aksum da ücretinde indirim yapmayı kabul etmeyen oyuncular arasında yer aldı. Çalışma saatlerinin uzunluğuna dikkat çeken Aksum, ücretinden en küçük bir indirim bile yapmayacağını söyledi.
Ücretinde indirim yapıp yapmayacağı sorulan İlker Aksum, konuya ilişkin tavrını net sözlerle ortaya koydu. Ünlü oyuncu, "Yüzde 0,01 bile indirim yok, ben kabul etmiyorum. Bazen 15-16 saat mesailer sürüyor. Bu dizi süreleri olduğu sürece bu ücretler dönecek" ifadelerini kullandı.
Uzun saatler süren set çalışmalarını gerekçe gösteren Aksum'un açıklaması, oyuncu ücretleri üzerinden yaşanan tartışmada dikkat çekti.
Dizi sektöründeki ekonomik sıkıntılar nedeniyle oyunculardan ücret indirimi talep edilmesi daha önce de gündeme gelmişti. Gazeteci Birsen Altuntaş'ın haberine göre, Kerem Alışık'ın başrolünde yer aldığı Haysiyet dizisinin yayın hayatını sürdürebilmesi için yapım şirketi, kanalın isteği üzerine oyunculardan yüzde 15 indirim talep etmişti.
Dizide Sadık Karlıova karakterini canlandıran Kerem Alışık'ın ise bu süreçte dikkat çeken bir öneride bulunduğu öne sürülmüştü. Ünlü oyuncunun, "İndirimi biz oyuncular yapalım, teknik ekibe dokunmayın" diyerek ücret kesintisinin set çalışanlarına yansıtılmamasını istediği aktarılmıştı. Alışık'ın bu çıkışı, sektörün yaşadığı ekonomik sıkıntılar karşısında teknik ekibin emeğine dikkat çekmişti.

Trip-hop tarzı müzik yapan dünyaca ünlü grubun üç albümü de son günlerde ülkede Spotify, Apple Music ve grubun YouTube sayfasında artık bulunmuyor.
Portishead'den Geoff Barrow, sosyal medya paylaşımında, İskoç müzisyen Annie Lennox'nun, Gazze'nin 2023 ve 2026 yıllarını gösteren bir paylaşımını yayımladı. Barrow gönderisine, "İnsanlar neden İsrail'i boykot ettiğimizi merak ediyor" diye yazdı.
"Soykırıma Müzik Yok" kampanyası, Birleşmiş Milletler'in Gazze'de soykırım olduğunu ilan etmesi üzerine, tepki olarak sanatçıları ve telif hakkı sahiplerini müziklerini İsrail'deki yayın platformlarından çekmeye teşvik eden kültürel bir boykot girişimi. Kampanyaya destek veren diğer önemli isimler arasında Björk, Lorde, IDLES, MUNA, Paloma Faith, Clairo, Wolf Alice, Lucy Dacus, AURORA, My Bloody Valentine, Denzel Curry, Shygirl, Paris Paloma, Vacations, Innervisions ve YHWH Nailgun yer alıyor.
Geçen yıl "Soykırıma Müzik Yok" grubu tarafından yayımlanan bir açıklamada, "Kültür, tek başına bombaları durduramaz, ancak siyasi baskının reddedilmesine yardımcı olabilir, kamuoyunu adalet yönünde değiştirebilir ve insanlığa karşı suç işleyen herhangi bir şirketin ya da ulusun sanat yoluyla aklanmasını ve normalleştirilmesini reddedebilir" denilmişti.
Birleşmiş Milletler tarafından atanan bir Soruşturma Komisyonu, Eylül 2025'te İsrail'in Gazze'deki Filistinlilere karşı soykırım işlediği sonucuna vardı. Uluslararası Af Örgütü de aynı sonuca ulaştığını ilan etti.
İsrail, soykırım yürüttüğü yönündeki suçlamaları sürekli olarak reddetti ve herhangi bir savaş suçu işlediğini inkar ederek, operasyonlarının 7 Ekim 2023'te Nova Müzik Festivali'nde Hamas'ın İsrail vatandaşlarına yönelik saldırısının ardından meşru bir meşru müdafaa eylemi olduğunu savundu. Noel-Williams, who plays for League Two side Barnet, has been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault by penetration, Hertfordshire Police said.
The 23-year-old, of High Oaks, St Albans, was remanded in custody following a hearing at Hatfield Magistrates' Court on Saturday.
In a statement, the club said it was "co-operating fully with authorities" and would determine further action "in due course".
Noel-Williams has also been charged with one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child, and one count of supplying a controlled (Class B) drug, police added.
In a statement, the London club said: "Barnet FC can confirm that first-team player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged and remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary.
"The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.
"As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment."
Noel-Williams, who previously played for Hemel Hempstead Town, Kettering Town, Matlock Town, Harrow Borough and Cheshunt, joined Barnet in June.

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points in the Women’s Super League after they made substitutions in four separate windows during their 1-0 victory over Everton in September.
Palace admitted breaching the competition’s rules and an independent tribunal ordered the points deduction, but no points will be awarded to Everton. It means Palace drop from 12th to 13th, below Birmingham City on goal difference. The match will not be replayed.
Palace made the substitutions during the second half and their 97th-minute introduction of Kirsty Howat, to replace Shannon O’Brien, was a breach of the rules. Teams have a maximum of three substitution windows per game, excluding half-time.
The WSL, Pro Ref and both clubs launched investigations. Promoted Palace led the opening-weekend game thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s 34th-minute goal and there were eight minutes of stoppage time indicated at the end.
The match officials who worked on the game were not appointed to any matches for the following round in the WSL and WSL2 in light of the incident.
The independent tribunal concluded Palace’s breach was inadvertent and that they had not tried to secure an unfair advantage. None of the parties involved are eligible to appeal.
Palace said: “Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate. We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL.”
Everton are also understood to be disappointed with the outcome but it is understood the club were not formally represented during the tribunal because the case was “The WSL versus Crystal Palace”. Everton wrote a letter to the tribunal which outlined their opinion that the introduction of Howat had a sporting impact.
Everton’s letter mentioned that they had accumulated seven shots after the 90th minute and 72% possession in stoppage time, indicating “that Everton were dominant and on top, chasing an equaliser” when the substitution broke the flow.
The Palace head coach, Jo Potter, told the tribunal that her assistant had suggested making the substitution.
The operations match manager’s report, submitted to the tribunal, stated the fourth official had not recorded Palace’s third substitution window in her notes because, when that was taking place in about the 90th minute, she was “simultaneously dealing with requests from the broadcast match manager, protests from both teams regarding decisions and added time, and the requirement to configure the added time for display on the fourth official’s board”.
Palace sit five points above the WSL’s automatic relegation place, having dropped from nine points to six. The side who finish 13th will play a relegation/promotion playoff against a WSL2 club.

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025
Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.
Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.
However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.
It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.
While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.
Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.
This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.
Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.
In a statement on their club website , external Palace said they were "disappointed" by the decision.
The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.
The rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match."
The tribunal said that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.
"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision. , external
They said the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.
It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".
Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.
Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.
"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."
Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

Freddie Potts has started all of Club Brugge's Champions League games
When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.
The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.
And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.
After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.
"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.
"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."
Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.
Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.
He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.
"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.
"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.
"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.
"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."
Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.
"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.
"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."
Freddie Potts on leaving West Ham, life in Belgium and beating Inter Milan
Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.
"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.
"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.
"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."
Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.
"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.
"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

Midfielder is preparing to face Liverpool after leaving the club he loves and overcoming a tough start in Belgium
I n April Freddie Potts was absorbing the disappointment of being substituted at half-time during West Ham’s FA Cup quarter-final defeat by Leeds. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later.
It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him.
“I thought this was the perfect place for me to take the next step,” Potts says of his move to the Belgian champions. “I’m not going to shy away – it was very hard. West Ham have been my club for my whole life. I still have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge.
“Every player wants to be in the team expected to win every week, and seeing how Club Brugge have performed in the Champions League before shows the project and how they want to develop the team and players. It was a very exciting place for me to come. They look to develop young players.”
Potts was six when he joined West Ham. His father, Steve, made 506 appearances for the club and is part of Scott Parker’s backroom staff there. His brother, Dan, came through the academy before moving to Luton in 2015. This is a West Ham family; it is not a surprise that moving to Belgium was emotional for Potts.
Yet it was the right move. Brugge are second in the Belgian Pro League, a point behind Union Saint-Gilloise, and have impressed in the Champions League. They have nine points from four games in the league phase and caused a stir when they beat Inter 4-3 at San Siro last month.
Potts calls it “one of the best nights of my career”. It was quite the turnaround for a player who mostly watched from the bench as West Ham tried to save themselves during the second half of last season. It helps that Potts knows how to stay calm. He was talked up as a future West Ham captain when he made his full debut and impressed in a 3-1 win over Newcastle last year. He had a run in the team but lost his place when Nuno switched to a 4-4-2 in January and settled on Mateus Fernandes and Tomas Soucek as his preferred partnership in central midfield.
That was when Potts remembered how he grew during loan spells at Portsmouth and Wycombe. “I know that you can have games where you feel like you are on top of the world, and then you can come straight back down,” he says. “The loans helped me out massively with West Ham because I managed to cope with the highs. The Newcastle game was a real high, but there were some lows after that and I feel like I was coping with it.”
Potts saw the reaction on social media when he left. Some West Ham fans were not happy with the club for allowing a homegrown player to depart. This season has been tough for West Ham, who are ninth in the Championship after a disappointing run and replaced Nuno with Parker this month. One problem has been the absence of a No 6. Potts, who can snap into a tackle and link play from deep, has been watching from afar.
“I still think they’re playing well,” he says. “They’ve got a great team, great players. I think Scott Parker is a really good manager and he’s got three teams promoted from the Championship. I don’t think it will be a problem again. West Ham will get promoted in the end.”
Potts has glitzier assignments and is adjusting to his surroundings. He cannot speak much Flemish but he has sipped a couple of Belgian beers and is enjoying life in Bruges. “I’m not going to lie, when I first joined I found it difficult. It’s completely different when you move country. But I was open to the challenge. At the start it was a challenge but now it’s really smooth.”
One of the biggest challenges has been adapting to a new style. Given the intensity of the Premier League it is a surprise to hear Potts say Brugge, managed by the 48-year-old Croatian Ivan Leko, have helped him become more physical.
“Straight away in training programmes it was a real surprise how hard everyone works,” Potts says. “It’s in the nature of the club to really work hard and give 100% every day. You see that straight away as you come in the door. No matter how hard it can be everyone gets on with it. No complaints. We’re a running team and everyone gives it their all. That’s the message from the top. It’s a real positive environment for someone of my age to be part of.”
Brugge have a couple of rising stars in attack: the rapid Portugal winger Carlos Forbs and the 22-year-old striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who scored a hat-trick in the win over Inter. There is a feeling Leko’s side could go on a run in Europe. They do not fear Liverpool. “It’ll be difficult for them coming to our place,” Potts says. “They’re a great team but we’re going to approach it like we have been doing with every game.
“Inter are one of the top teams in the competition. PSV are a great team and we got the win there. Liverpool will be tough but we’ve proved it against top teams before.”

Crystal Palace Women are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a win over Everton in September - the last of which came in the 97th minute - which is in breach of IFAB Laws that state clubs have no more than three substitution opportunities in each match
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Crystal Palace Women have been deducted three points in the WSL with immediate effect.
Promoted side Palace, who now drop into the relegation play-off spot, are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a 1-0 win over Everton in September.
This is in breach of IFAB Laws, which state clubs can make five substitutions, but have no more than three opportunities in each match to do so.
Palace made a substitution in a fourth window in the 97th minute of the match. Kirsty Howat, who was brought on for Shannon O'Brien, did not touch the ball before the full-time whistle was blown.
Palace admitted to the breach but felt the sanction sought by the WSL was "excessive", according to the written decisions published with the sanction.
However, the independent tribunal determined that a sporting sanction was necessary to avoid damaging the integrity of the competition.
In response, Palace said in a statement on Tuesday: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty - a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.
"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."
Everton's points total is unaffected by the sanction. They remain 11th in the table on 12 points after 11 matches. Palace, meanwhile, drop to second bottom, falling behind Birmingham on goal difference.
Everton disagreed with the assertion of Palace head coach Jo Potter that the outcome of the match was unaffected by their use of a fourth substitution window.
In a letter to the independent tribunal, Everton set out a four-point argument for how the non-compliant substitution had a direct sporting impact on the match.
"Palace did not make an extra substitution but used an extra substitution window, making changes in the 63rd, 83rd, 90th and, crucially, the 97th minute.
"This is devastating for Palace because Kirsty Howat, who came on for Shannon O'Brien, was only on the pitch for a matter of seconds and she didn't touch the ball.
"It is recognised [by the independent tribunal] that this hasn't created any advantage for Palace when it comes to the result, they have to deter other teams from choosing not to adhere to this rule.
"This will be upsetting for Palace, who have dropped down to second bottom in the table. The team in 14th at bottom of the table, currently Charlton, will be immediately relegated.
"Whoever is 13th goes into a play-off against the winner of a match between the second and third team in WSL 2.
"This is gutting for Palace, who were above Birmingham before this deduction. Now they've dropped down and they're in danger. And, mentally, we know how hard it is for promoted teams to stay in the WSL."

Kevin de Bruyne won 16 trophies in 10 years at Manchester City
Kevin de Bruyne's move to Napoli in 2025 was supposed to mark a continuation of his glittering decade at Manchester City as he approaches the twilight years of his career.
Instead, the midfielder, who is widely regarded as one of the standout players of his generation, has seen his time in Naples threaten to turn sour amid an early injury, friction with his team-mates and rumours of a January exit.
Napoli were Serie A champions in 2024-25 - the year before De Bruyne's arrival - but are currently languishing in eighth, while they sit 27th in the Champions League after a heavy 4-1 defeat at Porto earlier this month.
Belgium international De Bruyne lifted 16 trophies in his 10 years at City and is guaranteed a generous ovation when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday but the highs of his time in England are in contrast to the struggles he is seemingly enduring in Italy.
"Not a lot I can say for the moment," said De Bruyne when asked about his future. "I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.
"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening."
Statue, Pep's tears & a missed sitter - De Bruyne's emotional farewell
City decided not to renew De Bruyne's contract during the 2024-25 season and the player had the choice of heading to the US with Chicago Fire or staying in one of the top-five leagues in Europe.
The 35-year-old felt he could still cut it at the highest level but his first season at Napoli was heavily disrupted by a hamstring injury which kept him out for more than four months, restricting him to 21 appearances.
Napoli finished runners up to Inter Milan to lose their Serie A title and De Bruyne reportedly said , external he was "happy" manager Antonio Conte had departed in the summer as promises were not kept regarding the style of play.
But despite making his name as a technically gifted number 10, De Bruyne's role has been remodelled into a deeper holding one under Massimiliano Allegri in an ageing squad that has struggled this season.
In Porto, the fractures were clear to see, with De Bruyne having a heated on-field confrontation , external with striker Lorenzo Lucca and his team-mates were forced to step in to diffuse the situation.
The passionate side of De Bruyne's game was shown in Manchester too.
The midfielder shouted "shut up" at manager Pep Guardiola during a Champions League game against Real Madrid in 2023, and said "let me talk" when David Silva and Fernandinho were ushering him off the pitch at half-time shortly after he was booked against Napoli in 2017.
"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli," Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino tells BBC Sport. "The point is that the whole team is having difficulties.
"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.
"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show."
De Bruyne has played 16 times for Napoli this season - contributing four goals and two assists - but his long-term future at the club remains unclear.
In September, De Bruyne's wife reportedly , external told a Belgian publication about their desire to move back home, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as the player leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.
Asked if the quotes had been misinterpreted, De Bruyne said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.
"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.
"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family."
It has led to interest from the Netherlands with PSV Eindhoven making a £1.67m offer to sign him in January, but the two clubs are apart in their valuations as Napoli want up to £6.7m, according to Credendino.
"Napoli fans were not happy [with the interview]," he says. "There are many fans that say, 'OK, you can leave if you want, we are not putting chains on anybody'."
Napoli boss Allegri left the door open for a January exit by saying in his pre-match news conference the pair had "not spoken" about his future and it is "down to the players and who wants to leave" when the transfer window opens.
City manager Enzo Maresca was assistant to Pep Guardiola during the 2022-23 campaign in which De Bruyne helped the club to a Treble of trophies and the Italian has fond memories of the "fantastic season" they spent together.
"No doubt, [he is] one of the best," Maresca said of De Bruyne in his pre-match news conference. "Not only personally but also for the history of this club. In the last 10 years all the trophies the club achieved Kevin was here.
"He was an important player, a top guy, polite and for me it was a pleasure to work with him."
This is not the first time De Bruyne will be facing his former club with a reunion with City in the Champions League last season.
That trip turned out to be a bitterly unhappy experience, with De Bruyne substituted after 26 minutes following Giovanni di Lorenzo's red card in the 2-0 defeat.
The midfielder will be hoping for a better result on Tuesday as he aims to park his struggles for one evening.
City and Belgium winger Jeremy Doku said: "Kevin is someone that likes football. Even at this age he loves it.
"I don't have any doubts about his quality and I am sure everything will be fine in Napoli."

Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca
A s Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League .
In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions.
De Bruyne left for nothing in the summer of 2025 , but had fully returned the £55m City paid for him 10 years previously. Six Premier League titles, two FA Cups, five League Cups, a Club World Cup and that night in Istanbul when City conquered Inter, successes he will for ever cherish. Admittedly, the Belgian departed early that night in Turkey through injury, something he battled with in his later years in England.
Maresca was Guardiola’s assistant for the 2023 treble season, working closely with De Bruyne. “In the last 10 years, all the trophies the club achieved, Kevin was here and an important player, a fantastic player, a top guy, polite, fantastic,” he said. “It was a pleasure to work with him.”
His return may be made slightly more appealing because his powers have waned in Serie A and his teammates are not faring any better , although his compatriot Jérémy Doku said: “It’s fun to play with him. The quality he has is unbelievable, but we are all competitive so we all have to be on our best.”
At his peak, De Bruyne was the driving force for Guardiola, a two‑footed mercurial talent who could change a game in an instant. He was someone clearly more talented than most of the elite, able to glide past opponents, find a pass no one else could or just shift the ball from one foot to the other and smash in a goal from distance.
“I play more based on the feeling I have and where the space is, where I can feel I’m the most dangerous,” De Bruyne said on Monday. A reminder City do not possess someone of the same mould; even if Rayan Cherki may think he can be the heir, he is yet to consistently prove it.
“You always have to have courage to play football, you cannot only go long and just play for duels,” De Bruyne says of a style that evolved under Guardiola.
City have enjoyed these glorious talents for years; Yaya Touré could control a midfield, David Silva was able to control entire games. Maresca does not have access to someone like that and instead is attempting to create a unified team that makes the most of its expensive parts, but is yet to strike the perfect balance. For all of Erling Haaland’s incredible qualities as a striker, he cannot do it all by himself; he is reliant on service, something he is not getting from midfield or out wide.
Maresca tried the teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi alongside Elliot Anderson against Fulham on Saturday , leaving out the £125m summer signing Enzo Fernández .
Anderson was given a more attacking role, provided the sort of thrust De Bruyne often did. He does not possess the same technical expertise as the Belgian, although his volley may have earned a round of applause from his predecessor.
“It is not complicated, it is just a matter of knowing each other,” Maresca said. “I need to understand who is the ideal one for this kind of game and different kind of games. I don’t think it is just midfielders, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution.
“It’s part of the process. It is like a restart after 10 years with the same manager, same faces, same words, same methods. It’s not easy to change all of a sudden.”
Cherki is capable of amazing things, while Phil Foden infrequently threatens to rediscover his best form. De Bruyne, however, was part of a team that dominated. Often alongside Rodri and Ilkay Gündogan, the trio were almost the perfect balance of defensive diligence and attacking expertise, leaving opponents facing an nigh-on impossible task.
It is likely Maresca will change things for Napoli’s visit, with the ambition of a fourth win from five games in the Champions League , as City seek to secure progression as early as possible. Whichever team is put out, it will not have a talent like De Bruyne, meaning Maresca will have to work even harder to return to City’s Belgian-inspired peak.

Former Scottish FA president George Peat has died at the age of 86.
The former Airdrieonians and Stenhousemuir director spent four years in the role, taking over from John McBeth in 2007.
He oversaw the appointments of Scotland managers George Burley and Craig Levein and commissioned former first minister Henry McLeish to conduct a review of Scottish football.
Peat was also at the helm when Scottish referees opted to take strike action in November 2010.
"George loved his football and was renowned as a forthright personality and formidable negotiator but behind that imposing exterior lay a sharp wit and a glint in his eye," said current SFA president Mike Mulraney.
"He cared deeply about the national game and his beloved Airdrieonians.
"George was also passionate about the modernisation of the association and commissioned the McLeish Review of Scottish football as one of his first acts as president.
"He was a regular visitor to Hampden, even as his health deteriorated, and will be sadly missed by his friends and former colleagues at the Scottish FA and across the game."

Cav Miley has made 17 appearances since joining Chelmsford in the summer
Footballers may be among the fittest athletes in the world of sport, but they are not immune to bizarre injuries.
Dave Beasant famously severed a tendon in his big toe when he dropped a bottle of salad cream, while Rio Ferdinand strained tendons in his knee by lying in one position on the sofa for too long watching television.
The latest inductee into the strange injury hall of fame is Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley.
The 31-year-old midfielder missed the 2-2 draw with Walton and Hersham in the National League South on Saturday after twisting an ankle in training by falling down a badger hole.
Miley returned for the 1-0 home victory over Maidstone United on Monday, after which manager Mark Cooper shed more light on the incident.
"Everyone is telling me it's gone viral, but I told the truth - he fell down a badger hole," Cooper told the club's YouTube channel.
"I was told at the start it was a fox hole, but then the guy at where we train told me it's a badger hole.
"We need to make sure we fill all of them in before we train now."
Miley joined Chelmsford in the summer after spells in the National League with Southend United and Eastleigh.

An Olimpico tops the list of season highlights, with mention for Croix Bethune’s feats and a four-player nutmeg
S urely the final strands of gold and silver confetti have been picked out of the well worn surface of Audi Field in Washington by now. The Kansas City Current might not have left any unclaimed after their hard-earned NWSL championship , after outlasting a late threat from the Washington Spirit to claim a first title at their opponent’s friendly confines.
Before the annual onslaught of transfers and off-season rumblings fully heats up, we offer a quick look back at the NWSL season that was.
Let the record reflect that this writer spent the better part of an hour watching NWSL goal highlights in an attempt to stave off recency bias. But my word, what a hit from Vanessa DiBernardo to break Saturday’s championship-game deadlock.
Somewhat bafflingly, no reporters in the postgame news conference asked DiBernardo for her own account of the hit and how it felt. Suffice it to say that it must have felt exceptional, and not just due to the big-game moment.
Scoring an Olimpico is an incredibly rare feat, one of the few tricks that can elude even the game’s greatest players, from Marta to Messi. The right combination of weather conditions, angle, vertical trajectory, and helpful positioning by Kayla Sharples allowed this effort to dip into the tightest of windows between Sandy MacIver’s reach and the underside of the crossbar.
There’s good reason to think it may have been an intentional effort. Cloé Lacasse opened Utah’s semi-final against the Spirit with an Olimpico one week earlier, while Current left-back Izzy Rodríguez also tucked one against Bay FC in September. We may never know if it was premeditated or just a sublimely hit corner that fate nudged into the net. Let’s collectively assume it was, shall we?
Ashley Sanchez was a worthy MVP, winning the Golden Boot with 20 goals, the most ever scored by an American in a single NWSL season. And yet, the fact her North Carolina Courage narrowly missed the playoffs left the door open for other players who bolstered their cases in big games.
Players such as Croix Bethune . The midfielder requested a trade away from the Spirit in the off-season and certainly made the most of her move. Her first year in Kansas City began with a goal in her debut and she remained the creative heart of their best play, pulling the strings all the way through Saturday’s win at her former field. It’s a game her team might not have reached without her brilliant curling free-kick to shock Gotham in the semi-final.
Her partnership with Temwa Chawinga is a one-two tandem few opponents can match – and even fewer can contain.
This is far from the only honour appended to Bethune’s season, of course. Last week she was named the league’s midfielder of the year, also making the season-end Best XI. She also forced her way back into Emma Hayes’s US national team considerations for next summer’s World Cup in Brazil. We’ll soon see if and where she ranks in the Guardian’s annual list of the 100 best female footballers in the world.
The odds of nutmegging two people with one prod are already slim. Three players would make for a marvellous moment. But four players? All blissfully unaware as they talk among themselves after a shift of prematch work?
Gloating would seldom be more understandable, but Denver Summit midfielder Emma Regan took a more jubilant approach. By the time the ball scooted through her third teammate, a full wave of joyous bewilderment left her slack-jawed. As it meandered through a fourth, however, Regan could hardly stay upright, and who could blame her.

UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi tarihinde ilk kez iki Türk teknik direktör karşı karşıya gelecek.
Avrupa futbolunun kulüp düzeyindeki bir numaralı organizasyonunun 5. haftasında 25 Kasım Çarşamba günü oynanacak Shakhtar Donetsk-Fenerbahçe maçı, iki Türk teknik direktörün mücadelesine sahne olacak.
Ukrayna ekibi Shakhtar Donetsk'i çalıştıran Arda Turan ile Fenerbahçe'nin teknik direktörü Emre Belözoğlu, "Devler Ligi"nde karşılaşacak.
Shakhtar Donetsk-Fenerbahçe maçı, İngiltere'nin başkenti Londra'daki Stamford Bridge Stadı'nda oynanacak.
İngiliz hakem Michael Oliver'in yöneteceği karşılaşma TSİ 23.00'te başlayacak.
Sarı-lacivertli takım, Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde bu sezon 4 maçta 1 galibiyet, 2 beraberlik ve 1 yenilgi yaşadı.
Lig aşamasına sahasındaki Roma beraberliği (1-1) ile başlayan Fenerbahçe, ikinci haftada Aston Villa'ya deplasmanda farklı (6-0) mağlup oldu.
Üçüncü haftada Slavia Prag ile seyircisi önünde 2-2 berabere kalan sarı-lacivertliler, dördüncü maçında ise Liverpool'u 3-2 yenmeyi başardı.
Bu sonuçlarla 5 puan toplayan Fenerbahçe, 19 sırada kendine yer buldu.
Öte yandan 3 Kasım'da sarı-lacivertli takımın başına getirilen Emre Belözoğlu, teknik direktörlük kariyerinin ilk Şampiyonlar Ligi sınavını Arda Turan karşısında verecek.
Türk teknik adam Arda Turan'ın çalıştırdığı Shakhtar Donetsk, lig aşamasında 1 galibiyet, 1 beraberlik ve 2 yenilgi yaşadı.
Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde bu sezona PSV ile 1-1 berabere kalarak giriş yapan Shakhtar Donetsk, ikinci karşılaşmasında AEK'i 3-1 geçerek ilk 3 puanını aldı.
Üçüncü haftada Inter'e, dördüncü maçında ise Sporting'e 1-0'lık skorlarla kaybeden Ukrayna ekibi, 4 puan ve averajla 21. basamakta bulunuyor.
Arda Turan ile Emre Belözoğlu, uzun yıllar boyunca A Milli Futbol Takımı'nda birlikte mücadele etti.
Arda, A Milli Futbol Takımı'nda 2006-17 yılları arasında forma giyerken Emre, 2000-19 yılları arasında ay-yıldızlı formayı giydi.
İkili, 2012 yılında İspanya'nın köklü ekiplerinden Atletico Madrid'in forması altında da görev yaptı.
Emre Belözoğlu, 2012 yazında Fenerbahçe'den Atletico Madrid'e transfer olarak Arda Turan'ın takım arkadaşı oldu.

Ukrayna ekibi Shakhtar Donetsk, Tük takımlarıyla bugüne dek 10 kez karşı karşıya gelirken bu maçlarda yenilgi yaşamadı.
Sivasspor, Fenerbahçe, Başakşehir, Konyaspor ve Beşiktaş ile toplamda 10 maçta karşı karşıya gelen Shakhtar Donetsk, bu müsabakalarda 9 galibiyet elde ederken 1 maçta da sahadan beraberlikle ayrıldı.
Ukrayna ekibi bu maçlarda 21 gol kaydederken kalesinde 3 gol gördü.
Sarı-lacivertli kulüpten yapılan açıklamaya göre teknik direktör Emre Belözoğlu'nun belirlediği 22 kişilik kafilede şu isimler yer aldı:
Ederson Moraes, Mert Günok, Tarık Çetin, Nelson Semedo, Ognjen Mimovic, Milan Skriniar, Yiğit Efe Demir, Kojo Oppong, Levent Mercan, Mert Müldür, Archie Brown, N'Golo Kante, İsmail Yüksek, Matteo Guendouzi, Bartuğ Elmaz, Dorgeles Nene, Mason Greenwood, İrfan Can Kahveci, Oğuz Aydın, Kerem Aktürkoğlu, Romelu Lukaku, Vedat Muric.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.
